The Commentary on Sūrat al-Tawba (Tafsir Sūrat al-Tawba)

Know that this sūra is Medinan (madaniyya), and it is authentically related from the Prophet, through the transmission of al-Barā' ibn 'Āzib, that it is "the last sūra to be revealed in its entirety." It has many names.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbās that he was asked about this sūra and said: "It is al-Fāḍiḥa (the Disgracer). The revelation kept coming down with His saying [Exalted is He]: 'And among them, and among them,' until we thought that He would not leave any of us unmentioned." Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān said: "It is the sūra of punishment (sūrat al-'adhāb)."

It is well known that it is called Sūrat al-Buḥūth (the Sūra of Investigations). Among its names: al-Muba'thara (the Scattering-Forth); among its names: al-Munīra (the Illuminating); among its names: al-Ḥāfira (the Digging), because it dug out the hearts of the hypocrites. al-Naqqāsh narrated from Ibn 'Umar that it is called al-Muqashqisha (the Purifying). And from 'Imrān ibn Ḥudayr, who said: "I recited this sūra to a Bedouin, and he said: 'I think this sūra is the last thing revealed.' I said to him: 'Why?' He said: 'I see covenants being discarded and contracts being broken.'"

And from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr: this sūra was equal to Sūrat al-Baqara in length.

As for the discussion on the omission of the basmala: it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbās that he said: "I said to 'Uthmān, may Allah be pleased with him: 'What is the matter with you that you placed Sūrat al-Tawba, which is one of the mi'īn (sūras of about a hundred verses), and Sūrat al-Anfāl, which is one of the mathānī (the oft-repeated), side by side, and did not write the line ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾?' He said: 'When something of the Qur'an was revealed to the Messenger of Allah, he would call one of those who wrote, and say to him: "Place it in the sūra in which such-and-such is mentioned, place it in the sūra in which such-and-such is mentioned." Al-Anfāl was among the first things revealed in Medina, and al-Tawba was among the last things revealed, and their stories resembled one another, and the Messenger of Allah passed from this world without explaining to us anything about them, so we thought that they were one sūra. Therefore we joined them together and did not write ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾.'"

This report is in the Ṣaḥīḥ, related by Muslim. It is also reported that the Companions differed: some of them said: "They are two sūras," and some of them said: "They are one sūra." So they agreed to separate the two sūras with a blank space, and not to write "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."

A third opinion is what is related from Sufyān ibn 'Uyayna among the earlier scholars, and al-Mubarrad among the later ones: that the sūra is a sūra of the annulment of covenants and disavowal of the polytheists, and the basmala is a pledge of security and an opening of good; therefore they did not write "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿A disavowal from Allah and His Messenger﴾. His saying: ﴿disavowal (barā'a)﴾ — this is a disavowal (barā'a), and al-barā'a: the annulling of protection (naqḍ al-'iṣma). The meaning of the verse: a disavowal from Allah and His Messenger.

﴿to those with whom you made covenants among the polytheists﴾. Some of them said: Allah and His Messenger are free of the polytheists.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 2:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So travel freely in the land﴾ mean: come and go, go forth and return, and move about. ﴿For four months﴾. They differed concerning these four months.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: its beginning is the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), and its end is the tenth of Rabi al-Akhir. Al-Zuhri said: they are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qaʿdah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram.

The first opinion is the correct one.

The words of the Most High: ﴿And know that you cannot escape Allah﴾, meaning: you cannot escape Allah. Its meaning is that even though He grants you this period, He is not incapable of punishing you, as one who has lost something is incapable of reaching it. ﴿And that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾, meaning: He will humiliate the disbelievers.

The occasion of revelation of the verse: there were covenants and truces between the Messenger of Allah and the polytheists. When he went out on the expedition of Tabuk, the hypocrites spread rumours about the Prophet, so the polytheists began to break the covenants. It is said that this was before the expedition of Tabuk. When the ninth year after the Hijrah came, he sent Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) to lead the people in the pilgrimage, and he sent ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) to recite to the people these verses from the beginning of this surah. It is narrated that he first sent Abu Bakr, then he sent ʿAli after him and said: "None should convey these verses except a man from me," meaning from my kin. So Abu Bakr was the commander over the season, and ʿAli would proclaim these verses among the people.

It is narrated that ʿAli was asked: "With what did the Messenger of Allah send you?" He said: "He sent me with four things: first, whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of Allah, its term extends to four months; second, no polytheist may perform the pilgrimage after this year; third, no one may circumambulate the House naked; fourth, no one enters Paradise except a believing soul."

If someone says: how did he send Abu Bakr with these verses and then dismiss him and send ʿAli, saying: "None should convey on my behalf except a man from me"? If none may convey this except a man of his kin, then the same applies to all the other matters?

The answer to this: the scholars have mentioned that the Messenger of Allah did not dismiss Abu Bakr from the season; he remained the commander. He only sent ʿAli to proclaim these verses, because the Arabs had established a custom that a covenant is concluded only by the chief of a people, and a covenant is annulled only by their chief or a man of his household. So he sent ʿAli according to what they had agreed upon, in order to remove the excuses completely, so that no excuse would remain for them. This was the meaning, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: a notification from Allah and His Messenger. Al-Harith ibn Hilliza said:

(Asma' has notified us of the parting between us, though a lord who dwells long wearies of the dwelling.)

Its meaning: she informed us.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿to the people on the day of the greater Hajj﴾ — the scholars differed concerning "the day of the greater Hajj" (al-hajj al-akbar), with several opinions:

Yahya ibn al-Jazzar reported that Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, went out on the day of the 'Id on a mount, and a man seized the bridle of his mount and said: "What is the day of the greater Hajj?" He said: "It is the day you are in now; let go of it."

A similar report is transmitted from Ibn 'Umar, al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, and Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa.

The second opinion is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: it is the day of 'Arafa. This is the view of Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, and a group.

Ibn Sirin said — and this is the third opinion: the day of the greater Hajj is the day on which the Messenger of Allah performed Hajj, a day on which the Hajj of all the nations coincided.

The sound view is one of the first two opinions.

The scholars differed concerning "the greater Hajj" (al-hajj al-akbar):

One of the two opinions is that the greater Hajj is the Qur'an, and the lesser Hajj is the ifrad (performing Hajj alone, without 'Umra).

The second opinion is that the greater Hajj is the Hajj itself, and the lesser is the 'Umra.

His saying: ﴿That Allah is free from obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger. So if you repent, it is better for you; but if you turn away, then know that you will not cause failure to Allah. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾ — its meaning: and His Messenger is also free from obligation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 4:

﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists﴾. The exception applies to a group of the Banu Damrah. Allah commanded His Messenger to fulfil their covenant with them until its term, and nine months of their term remained. The reason for completing it is that they had not broken the covenant, and this is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿then they have not fallen short of you in anything﴾. ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār recited: "thumma lam yandiḍūkum shay'an" with the letter ḍād (ض) dotted, i.e., "thumma lam yanquḍūkum shay'an" (they did not breach with you in anything).

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿and they have not supported anyone against you﴾. Its meaning: they have not aided anyone against you. ﴿So complete for them their covenant until its term. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous﴾. That is, those who are righteous (al-muttaqūn) by refraining from breaking the covenant. It is related from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "The righteous (al-muttaqī) is one who abandons what is not harmful out of caution regarding what is harmful."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 5:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists﴾. It is narrated in the books of tafsir that the Prophet (ﷺ) set a term for the polytheists who had a treaty (ʿahd) between them and the Prophet of four months, and a term for those who had no treaty between them and the Messenger of God the remainder of Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram, which is fifty nights. This is the meaning of the verse.

If it is said: He, the Exalted, said "when the sacred months have passed," but what you have mentioned is only part of the sacred months.

We say: this portion was contiguous with what had passed, so the name of the whole was applied to it. Its meaning is: the well-known period that follows the passing of the sacred months has elapsed.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾. Its meaning is known.

His words ﴿and seize them﴾ are clear, that is: seize them as captives. The Arabs call a captive akhidh (one seized), and in the proverb: "More lying than an akhidh."

His words, the Exalted: ﴿and besiege them﴾, meaning: imprison them, that is: prevent them from reaching between them and the Sacred Mosque. This is the meaning of ḥabs (confinement) here.

And His words: ﴿and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾. Abu ʿUbayda said: al-marsad (the place of ambush) means the roads. That is: lie in wait for them on the roads of Makkah so that they do not reach the Sacred Mosque. The poet said:

(And I have known well [and I do not think you are forgetful] ... that death for the youth is at the ambush.)

His words: ﴿But if they repent﴾, meaning: they believe, ﴿and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go their way﴾, meaning: let them go their way to reach the Sacred Mosque. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ is known.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 6:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection﴾. Al-istijarah (seeking protection, asylum) means seeking safety (aman). The meaning of the verse: if any one of the polytheists asks you for protection, then grant him protection, i.e., give him security, ﴿until he hears the words of Allah﴾, meaning: concerning what is for him and against him of punishment and reward, and promise and warning. ﴿Then convey him to his place of safety﴾, meaning: the place where he will be secure. ﴿That is because they are a people who do not know﴾. Its meaning: they need to hear the words of Allah the Most High because of their ignorance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How can there be a covenant with Allah and with His Messenger for the polytheists?﴾ Al-Farra' said: The word "kayfa" (how) here is an interrogative used in the sense of denial, and its meaning is: there shall not be a covenant for the polytheists with Allah and with His Messenger, that is, nor with His Messenger.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ These are a people from the Banu Dhamrah, as we have mentioned.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So as long as they are upright toward you, be upright toward them﴾ meaning: if they fulfill their covenant with you, then fulfill your covenant with them. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the righteous﴾. It was said its meaning is: indeed Allah loves the believers. And it was said: Allah loves the righteous, meaning those who do not break the covenant.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How (can there be a covenant), when if they gain the upper hand over you they will not observe regarding you any kinship (ill) or pact (dhimmah)?﴾ That is: how can they have a covenant, when if they gain the upper hand over you they will not observe regarding you any kinship (ill) or pact (dhimmah)? Opinions have differed concerning "ill" (illa):

It is narrated from Mujahid that "illa" here means Allah, exalted is He. And in the non-canonical readings it was recited: "lā yarqubū fīkum īlan wa-lā dhimmah," where "īl" means Allah.

It is narrated from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said regarding the words of Musaylimah the liar, may Allah curse him, when he heard him say: "O frog, croak, croak, how much will you croak? You do not muddy the water, nor do you prevent the drink." Abu Bakr said: "Indeed, this is speech that did not come from il", meaning from Allah.

The second opinion is that of Abu 'Ubayda: "al-il" is the covenant, and "al-dhimmah" is the obligation of protection.

The third is the view of al-Dahhak, which is the best and most preferred of the opinions. He said: "al-il" is kinship, and "al-dhimmah" is the covenant. Hassan ibn Thabit said:

(By your life, your kinship with Quraysh is like the kinship of a young camel to an ostrich's chick.)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They please you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse﴾ That is: they promise fulfillment with words, but their hearts refuse anything except treachery. ﴿And most of them are defiant transgressors.﴾ If someone says: this refers to the polytheists, and they are all defiant transgressors, so how does He say "most of them"?

We say: "fisq" (defiance) here means breaking the covenant, and among the polytheists there were those who fulfilled their covenant; therefore He said, ﴿and most of them are defiant transgressors.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 9:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿They have sold the signs of Allah for a small price﴾ — the verse. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The world with all its treasures is a small price." The meaning of the verse is that they chose the world over the pleasure of Allah and over belief in the signs of Allah. ﴿And they have averted [others] from His way﴾ — meaning they prevented people from His way. ﴿Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾ — the meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They do not observe regarding a believer any tie of kinship or covenant of protection﴾. *Al-murāqaba* (مراقبة) means *al-ḥifẓ* (حفظ), guarding and preserving. As for *al-il* (إل) and *al-dhimma* (ذمة), we have already explained their meanings. ﴿And it is they who are the transgressors﴾, those who go beyond the limits.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if they repent, establish the prayer, and give the zakat, then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 12:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant﴾. This refers to the covenant that existed between the Messenger of God and the Quraysh. They broke the covenant, and their breach was that they aided the Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah. The Banu Bakr were allies of the Quraysh, and Khuza'ah were allies of the Prophet. A man from Khuza'ah came to the Prophet in al-Madinah and recited to him:

(O God, I appeal to Muhammad, the oath of our father and his father, the ancient one...)

(And that the Quraysh have broken the promise to you, and attacked us by night at al-Watir while we slept...)

(And they killed us while we were bowing and prostrating...)

in many verses. The Messenger of God said: "You shall be victorious, if I do not support you."

It is also related that he saw a cloud flashing, and the Messenger of God said: "Indeed this cloud heralds the victory of Khuza'ah." This was the beginning of the intention to conquer Makkah.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And they revile your religion﴾. This is evidence that if a dhimmi openly reviles the religion of Islam, he has no covenant left, and it is permissible to kill him.

His words: ﴿So fight the leaders of disbelief﴾, meaning: the heads of disbelief. The heads of disbelief were: Abu Sufyan, Suhayl ibn 'Amr, Umayyah ibn Safwan, and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl. ﴿Indeed they have no oaths﴾, meaning: they have no covenants. Al-Hasan al-Basri recited: "Indeed they have no faith (iman)," and this is the choice of Ibn 'Amir. It is also possible that "oaths" here carries the meaning of "faith," as the Arabs say: "amantuhu imanan" (I secured him with a pledge of safety), so the verbal noun is mentioned and the noun is intended. ﴿So that they may desist﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 13:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths﴾ — its meaning is well known.

His words ﴿and they plotted to expel the Messenger﴾ — this is well known. ﴿And they were the first to attack you﴾ — by this He means that they began the fighting at the battle of Badr. Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him, said: "We will not return until we uproot Muhammad and his companions." ﴿Do you fear them? Allah has more right that you fear Him, if you are believers﴾ — its meaning is: clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 9, verse 14:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, give you victory over them﴾. The meaning of the verse is apparent.

And His words: ﴿and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾ mean: Khuza'a.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 15:

﴿And He will remove the rage from their hearts﴾, meaning: Khuza'ah. {And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills, and Allah is Knowing, Wise.} It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said on the day of the Conquest of Makkah: "Lift the sword, except from Khuza'ah, from the Banu Bakr, until the afternoon (al-'asr)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 16:

Regarding His the Exalted's saying: ﴿Or did you think that you would be left alone while Allah has not yet known those among you who strive (jahadu) [in the way of Allah]﴾, and so on. The people of tafsir (ahl al-tafsir) said: When Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet to fight, the hypocrites (al-munafiqun) came to light, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿Or did you think that you would be left alone while Allah has not yet known those among you who strive﴾. The meaning of "knowledge" here is the knowledge upon which reward is based, which is knowledge after existence (al-'ilm ba'da al-wujud), not the knowledge of the unseen (ilm al-ghayb) upon which reward is not based. ﴿While Allah has not yet known﴾, meaning: and Allah has not yet known. ﴿And have not taken, other than Allah and His Messenger and the believers, an intimate (waliyjah)﴾. Al-Farra' said: The waliyjah is the bitana (inner confidant), which is the person to whom a man reveals his secret, so the meaning of the verse becomes: ﴿while Allah has not yet known﴾, and Allah has not yet known those among you who strive, and has not known those who refrained from taking, other than Allah and His Messenger and the believers, an intimate. ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾ is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 17:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah﴾. The meaning of the verse: the denial of the fitness (ahliyyah) of the polytheists to maintain the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram).

The words ﴿testifying against themselves to disbelief﴾: "testifying" (shahidin) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). As for their testifying against themselves to disbelief, it is their prostration to the idols and their saying in the talbiyah: "Here I am, O Allah, here I am; You have no partner, except a partner who is Yours, You possess him and what he possesses."

There is another opinion regarding His words ﴿testifying against themselves to disbelief﴾: that it means you say to the Jew: "What are you?" and he says: "A Jew." And you say to the Christian: "What are you?" and he says: "A Christian." Likewise the Magian and the polytheist.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Those—their deeds have become void, and in the Fire they will abide eternally﴾. Ḥubūṭ (voiding, nullification, gloss: the nullification of deeds) is nullification, and khalidun (abiding eternally) means lasting.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 18:

God's words: ﴿Only those who believe in God and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakat, and fear none but God, shall maintain the mosques of God﴾ (Q 9:18). The occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of the verse: when al-'Abbas (may God be pleased with him) was taken captive on the day of Badr, the Companions of the Messenger of God reproached him for abandoning Islam and emigration (hijrah). He said: "We are the maintainers of the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) and the givers of water to the pilgrims (saqat al-hujjaj)."

According to another narration: when he embraced Islam, he said to the Muslims: "If you have preceded us in Islam, we were indeed maintaining the Sacred Mosque and giving water to the pilgrims." So God the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿Only those who believe in God and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakat, and fear none but God, shall maintain the mosques of God﴾. Its meaning: he did not abandon belief in God out of fear of anyone. ﴿It is hoped that those will be among the guided﴾. "Hope" ('asa) from God is binding. If someone says: Do you claim that everyone who maintains a mosque, in the manner God described, is [a believer]?

We say: the meaning of the verse, and God knows best, is that whoever possesses these attributes is among the people who maintain the Sacred Mosque, and none maintains the Sacred Mosque except one who combines these attributes. The maintenance of the Sacred Mosque is by remembrance of God, turning towards Him, supplication, prayer, and other things.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the way of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah.﴾ Most of the exegetes hold that this verse was revealed concerning ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both. The one who reproached al-ʿAbbās for abandoning Islam and emigration was ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-ʿAbbās said: "We are the custodians of the Sacred Mosque and the providers of water to the pilgrims." So Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims...﴾ Its meaning is: Do you consider the people who provide water for the pilgrims and the people who maintain the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in Allah? It has also been recited: "Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims and the ʿUmrah of the Sacred Mosque..." On this recitation there is no need to supply the word "people" (ahl). ﴿They are not equal in the sight of Allah﴾ means: one who worships Allah while being a believer is not equal to one who maintains the mosque while being a polytheist. ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ Reports have come concerning the encouragement to maintain the mosques:

Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When you see a man frequenting the mosques, bear witness to his faith." Then he recited the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Only those maintain the mosques of Allah who believe in Allah...﴾

Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever goes out or comes to the mosque, Allah prepares for him a welcome gift every time he goes out or comes."

Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The mosque is a marketplace of the Garden. Whoever enters it is the guest of Allah; his hospitality is forgiveness, and his greeting is honour. When you enter, then graze (fa-irtaʿū)." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is ir-tiʿā (grazing)?" He said: "Supplication to Allah and desire for Him."

It is authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah builds for him one like it in the Garden."

And in the narration of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever builds a mosque, even as small as the nest of a sandgrouse, Allah builds for him a house in the Garden."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 20:

Concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who believed and emigrated and strove in the way of Allah with their wealth and their selves are greater in rank with Allah﴾. If someone says: How does His saying ﴿greater in rank with Allah﴾ hold, when the polytheists have no rank at all? The answer is in two respects:

The first: it is greater than their rank by their own reckoning concerning themselves. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that day are better in their resting place and finer in their resting at noon﴾, and its meaning is: by their own reckoning concerning themselves.

The second: that this category of believers is greater in rank with Allah than others.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those are the triumphant.﴾ The triumphant (al-fa'iz) is the one who has attained his desire.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Their Lord gives them glad tidings of mercy from Him, and approval, and gardens for them wherein is enduring bliss﴾ — the verse, and so on.

Al-bushara (glad tidings) is a true report of good news; it is called bushara because the complexion of the face changes by it (bashara).

As for His words ﴿of mercy from Him and approval, and gardens for them wherein is enduring bliss﴾: al-na'im is the pleasant living, and al-muqim is the lasting one, that which never departs (la yazha'n abadan).
﴿Abiding therein forever. Indeed, with Allah is a great reward.﴾ Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 23:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies﴾ to the end of the verse. The verse was revealed concerning a people who embraced Islam in Makkah, but when the Muslims emigrated (hijrah), they did not emigrate.

Ibn 'Abbas said: When a man intended to emigrate, his family and children would cling to him and say, "Will you abandon us and leave us?" So he would stay out of compassion for them. Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿If they prefer disbelief over faith﴾ its meaning is: that is, they chose disbelief over faith.

His saying: ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then those are the wrongdoers﴾. At that time, faith was not accepted except from one who had emigrated. So this is the meaning of the Almighty's saying: ﴿then those are the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 24:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses﴾. It is narrated that when the first part of this verse was revealed, those who had embraced Islam but had not emigrated said: "If we emigrate, our wealth will be lost, our homes will be ruined, and we will sever our ties of kinship." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and your clan﴾. It has been recited in two readings: "ʿashīratukum" (your clan) and "ʿashīrātukum" (your clans). The more correct is "ʿashīratukum," since the plural of ʿashīra (clan) is ʿashāʾir, and ʿashīrāt, they said, is weak in the Arabic language.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and wealth you have acquired﴾. That is, that which you have earned (ukhtasabtumūhā). Similar to it is the words of Allah the Exalted: {And whoever earns (yaqtarif) a good deed}, meaning: earns (yaktasib).

His words: ﴿and commerce, the decline of which you fear﴾. Its meaning is clear.

It is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak that he said concerning His words: ﴿and commerce, the decline of which you fear﴾: "It refers to sisters and daughters when no suitor is found for them." This was related by al-Naqqāsh in his tafsir.

His words: ﴿and dwellings with which you are pleased﴾, meaning: that you find pleasant.

His words: ﴿are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait﴾. Its meaning: then wait.

His words ﴿until Allah brings His command﴾. Most of the exegetes hold that what is meant by it is the conquest of Mecca. This is a command of threat, and it is neither a binding command, nor a recommendation, nor a permission.

His words: ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾. Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Certainly, Allah has given you victory on many battlefields, and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you⦆ – the verse. Hunayn is a valley between Makkah and al-Ta'if. ﴿When your great number pleased you⦆: it is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) was with twelve thousand men, while the polytheists were four thousand, commanded by Malik ibn 'Awf al-Nasri. A man from the Ansar called Salamah ibn Salamah ibn Waqsh said: "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers." Allah, may He be exalted, did not approve of his saying, and left them to themselves. The polytheists charged in one assault, and all the Muslims were routed except a small band who remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), among them al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib.

Al-Bukhari mentioned in al-Sahih, on the authority of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: "Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith was holding the bridle of the Prophet's mule on the day of Hunayn, while the Prophet (ﷺ) was saying: 'I am the Prophet, there is no lie. I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib.'" Then al-'Abbas – may Allah be pleased with him – called out to the Muslims on the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) – and he was a man with a loud voice – so he began calling: "O companions of Surat al-Baqarah! O helpers of Allah and helpers of His Messenger! O companions of the tree! This is the Messenger of Allah!" So they returned and fought, and the defeat fell upon the disbelievers... the story to its end." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it availed you nothing⦆, meaning: victory does not come through numbers, but through the help of Allah, may He be exalted.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and the earth, for all its vastness, became constricted for you⦆. Al-Farra' said: the "ba'" here carries the sense of "fi" (in), meaning: in its vastness and breadth. It was also said the meaning is: with its vastness and breadth.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿then you turned back in retreat⦆, i.e., scattering, meaning: defeated.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then God sent down His tranquility (sakinah) upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾ – the verse. Al-sakinah: mercy. It was also said: al-sakinah is security (al-amanah). It is a form (fa'ilah) derived from al-sukun (stillness), and here it carries the meaning of victory (al-nasr). The poet said:

(By God, a grave in al-Basitah has taken him; what did it conceal of tranquility and dignity?)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He sent down hosts you did not see﴾ – meaning: the angels. They were sent down not for fighting, but to strike terror into the disbelievers and to encourage the Muslims, for it is related that the angels did not fight except on the day of Badr.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He punished those who disbelieved﴾ – meaning: by killing and capture. ﴿And that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾ – its meaning is clear.
Allah's words: ﴿Then Allah will turn in forgiveness after that to whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Its meaning is clear, and this refers to those who ceased from killing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 28:

The words of the Most High: ﴿O you who have believed, the polytheists are [but] impure (najas)﴾. The meaning of His words ﴿impure (najas)﴾ is filth (qadhar). When it is joined to something else it is said: "rijs najs" (filthy impurity); and when it stands alone it is said: "najs."

It is narrated from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he said: "Their impurity is like the impurity of the dog and the pig."

And from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: "If a Muslim shakes hands with a disbeliever, it is obligatory upon him to wash his hand."

The sound view is that what is meant by the verse is that avoidance of them is obligatory, just as avoidance of impurities is obligatory. It has also been said that the meaning of His words ﴿impure (najs)﴾ is that they are in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) and do not perform ghusl, and they incur minor impurity (hadath) and do not perform wudu'.

The words of the Most High: ﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs﴾. This is a report in the form of a command, and its meaning is: do not allow them to enter the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs.

The school of the people of Madina holds that the Sacred Mosque is the entire Haram, and no disbeliever is left to enter it, even if he is a treaty-holder (mu'ahid) or a slave. This is the view of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and a group [of scholars].

The school of the Kufans holds that a treaty-holder and a slave may be permitted to enter it, and this is narrated from Jabir.

As for His words ﴿And if you fear poverty (ʿaylah)﴾, it means: poverty (faqr). In the codex of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, the reading is: "wa in khiftum ʿaʾilah," meaning: a burdensome matter. It is said: ʿalaniy al-amr, i.e., it was hard upon me.

The occasion of revelation of the verse: the livelihood of the people of Makka was only from trade and profits. When Allah the Most High commanded the Muslims not to allow the disbelievers to enter the Sacred Mosque, they said: "How then will our livelihood be?" They feared poverty and narrowness of living. So Allah the Most High said to them: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will soon enrich you from His bounty, if He wills﴾. It is related that the people of Jurash (with a dotted jim) and Sanaʾ, and all the other regions of Yemen, embraced Islam and brought abundant provisions to the people of Makka, and Allah widened [their livelihood] for them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾. Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 29:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden﴾. If someone says: "The People of the Two Books believe in Allah and the Last Day, so what is the meaning of the verse?"

The answer has two aspects:

The first: They do not believe in Allah and the Last Day in the way the believers do, for they say: "Uzayr is the son of Allah," and they say: "The Messiah is the son of Allah," and the Jews said: "There is no eating and no drinking in Paradise."

The second answer: their disbelief is like the disbelief of one who does not believe in Allah and the Last Day, in the greatness of the sin.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and do not adopt the religion of truth﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: "and do not obey Allah in the manner of the people of truth."

His words: ﴿from those who were given the Book, until they pay the jizya willingly while they are humbled﴾. Qatada said: "'An yad" (willingly/from a hand): from subjugation and humiliation. Others said: "'An yad" means: they give it with their own hand. And there is a third view: "'An yad" means: by acknowledging the favour of the people of Islam upon them. ﴿while they are humbled﴾. It is narrated from Salman al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: its meaning is: "while they are despised." And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: he is seized and struck on the neck; this is the meaning of humiliation (sagar). Others said: it is taken from him while he stands and the one taking it sits. It was also said: he is grabbed by the collar and dragged roughly to the place of payment. According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, the meaning of humiliation is: the application of the rulings of Islam over them. And this is a good meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 30:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of God."﴾ This refers to specific people who were in Medina, whom the sword destroyed. Among them were Sallam ibn Mishkam, Malik ibn al-Ḍayf, and Finhas the Jew. As for now, none of them says this. It is also said that those who uttered this statement were a people from their predecessors and forefathers.

The reason for this is that when the Jews altered (the Torah) and opposed the law of the Torah, God Most High removed the Torah from their hearts. Ezra went out wandering through the land seeking knowledge, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) met him and taught him the Torah. It is also related that a light descended and entered his body, and he recited the Torah from memory. He returned and dictated the Torah to the Jews, and a group of them said this statement, meaning: Ezra is the son of God.

﴿And the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of God."﴾ They hold to this now.

His saying: ﴿That is their saying with their mouths.﴾ If someone says: a person does not say a statement except with his mouth, so how is the meaning of this statement?

The answer: its meaning is that they uttered this statement without any proof, clarification, or evidence; it was merely a bare statement without foundation.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Imitating﴾ (yuḍāhi'ūna). It has been read in two ways. The word ﴿yuḍāhi'ūna﴾ means: they resemble, and al-muḍāhāh means similarity and likeness. The Arabs say: "imra'a ḍahyā'" when a woman does not menstruate, for she resembles men.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The saying of those who disbelieved before﴾ has two meanings:

One of them: the saying of those who associated partners before; for the polytheists used to say: Manāt, al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā are the daughters of God.

The second statement: the Christians said about the Messiah what the Jews said about Ezra. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before.﴾

﴿May God fight them﴾. Abu ʿUbayda said: "May God curse them." It was also said: "God has destroyed them," as the Arabs say: "ʿafāhu Allāh," meaning: "aʿfāhu Allāh" (may God grant him well-being).

There is also a third view: that this is an expression of wonder, as the poet said:

(Oh, may God fight Layla, how she amazes me... and she tells people that I do not care for her.)

The meaning is not the literal fact of fighting, but rather it is an expression of wonder.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿How are they turned away?﴾ Its meaning is: how are they turned away? It is said: "arḍ ma'fūka" when rain is diverted from it, and "qawl ma'fūk" when it is diverted from the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 31:

The Almighty's saying, ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾. It is said: the rabbis (al-ahbar) are from among the Jews, and the monks (al-ruhban) are from among the Christians, and we have already explained the views on these terms earlier. If someone says: "They did not worship the rabbis and the monks, so what is the meaning of His saying, ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾?"

We say: its meaning is that they declared lawful what they (the rabbis and monks) declared lawful, and forbidden what they declared forbidden; this is the meaning of their worship of them. This meaning has been authenticated through the narration of 'Adi ibn Hatim, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

As for His saying, ﴿And the Messiah, son of Mary, though they were only commanded to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾, its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 32:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾. Its meaning: they wish to extinguish (yukhmidu) the light of Allah. The intended meaning of "the light" is the Qur'an. It was also said: it is Muhammad (ﷺ).

His saying: ﴿with their mouths﴾ means: with their denial.

His saying: ﴿But Allah refuses except that He complete His light, even if the disbelievers dislike it﴾: its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 33:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.﴾ The exegetes (al-Mufassirun) said: This refers to the time of the descent of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, when no one will remain on the earth except that he will embrace Islam.

And regarding His words ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾, there is another opinion, namely that the prevailing is by argument (al-izhar bil-hujjah); so the religion of Islam is manifest over all other religions through proof and argument.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 34:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis (al-ahbar) and the monks (al-ruhban) consume the wealth of people in falsehood and bar [them] from the way of Allah﴾, the verse. We have already explained the meaning of al-ahbar and al-ruhban earlier. As for His words ﴿consume the wealth of people in falsehood﴾, the people of tafsir said: what is meant by it is taking bribes in judgments and the provisions that their scholars were given by their common folk. ﴿And bar [them] from the way of Allah﴾ means: they prevent people from Islam. As for His words ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah﴾, al-kanz (hoarding, treasure) is wealth that has been accumulated. The poet said:

(By my worth, if I feed their guest, I scrape the bottom of the barrel of dates (al-hata), while with me the wheat is stored (maknuz).)

They said: al-hatai is the dried date that has been crushed/ the poor-quality dates (al-muqill), i.e., the one who has little.

The people of knowledge differed regarding who this verse was revealed about. Some of them said: it was revealed about the People of the Book, while most of them said it was revealed about all of them.

They differed concerning al-kanz. It is narrated from Ibn Umar and a group [of scholars] that al-kanz is every wealth whose zakat has not been paid; but wealth whose zakat has been paid is not a treasure, even if it is buried. It is narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: four thousand dirhams as expenditure and what is above it is a treasure. Some of them said: whatever exceeds the need is a treasure.

As for His words ﴿and do not spend them in the way of Allah﴾: if a questioner asks and says: the gold and silver have both been mentioned together, so how does He say "and do not spend them" and not "and do not spend them both"?

The answer to this is in two respects:

The first: the meaning is "and do not spend the treasures (al-kunuz) in the way of Allah."

The second: the meaning of the verse is: they hoard gold and do not spend it, and they hoard silver and do not spend it, so one of them has been sufficient in place of the other. The poet said:

(We are content with what we have, and you are content with what you have, though our opinions differ.)

Its meaning: we are content with what we have, and you are content with what you have. A similar usage is the poet's saying:

(If the freshness of youth and black hair are not [kept] in check, they become madness.)

Meaning: as long as they are not kept in check (lam yu'ada) — i.e., both.

His words ﴿so give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾: its meaning is: place this threat in the position of good news, for otherwise a threat is not, in reality, glad tidings.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day it will be heated in the fire of Hell﴾, meaning: it will be kindled over them until it becomes fire.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with it﴾. The people of tafsir said: a dirham is not placed in the place of a dirham, nor a dinar in the place of a dinar; rather, the skin is enlarged so that every dinar and dirham is placed in its own place.

In the hadith of Abu Umamah al-Bahili (may Allah be pleased with him): "A man from the People of the Bench (ahl al-Suffah) died and left a dinar, and the Prophet said: 'A brand.' Another died and left two dinars, and he said: 'Two brands.'"

It is also authentically related from the Prophet that he said: "Gold and silver will be made into plates, and with them they will be branded every day, a day whose measure is fifty thousand years, then he will see his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire."

Thawban narrated: "When Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims with great hardship. They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, which wealth should we acquire, when concerning wealth what has been revealed has been revealed?' He said: 'Let one of you acquire a grateful heart, a remembering tongue, and a wife who helps him in his religion.'"

﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred. That is the upright religion. So do not wrong yourselves therein, and fight the polytheists all together.﴾

Also in the reports from the Prophet: "The treasure will follow its owner until it bites his hand and he chews it off, then it follows the rest of his body."

It has been related from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (may Allah have mercy on him) that he said: the verse is abrogated by the verse of zakat. The rest of the scholars said: it is not abrogated. And from Abu Bakr al-Warraq (may Allah have mercy on him) that he said: He only mentioned the forehead, the side and the back because the wealthy man, when he sees the poor man, contracts his forehead, draws together what is between his eyes, turns his back to him, and turns his side away from him.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.﴾ This is a warning and a threat.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah﴾. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: the meaning of the verse is that the months by which the Muslims worship in their fasting, their pilgrimage, their festivals and all their other affairs are the lunar months (bi-l-ahilla). The people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) used to reckon the year by solar months, and they made the year three hundred and sixty-five days and a quarter of a day. As for the Shari'ah, the year is what we have explained, and for this reason fasting falls at one time in winter and at another time in summer.

His saying: ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾, i.e., in the decree of Allah. It was also said: in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). ﴿The day He created the heavens and the earth﴾: the meaning is clear.

His saying: ﴿Of them, four are sacred﴾. They are: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram, and Rajab. One is solitary and three are consecutive (sarad).

It is authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ), through the narration of Abu Bakrah, that he said: "Behold, time has revolved to its original state on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred..." and the report continues.

His saying: ﴿That is the upright religion﴾, i.e., that is the correct reckoning.

His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾. Scholars differed on this in two opinions:

The first: that His saying ﴿so do not wrong therein﴾ refers to the four sacred months.

The second: that it refers to all the months of the year, and this is related from Ibn 'Abbas.

As for wrongdoing (zulm) in this context, it is the abandonment of obedience and the commission of disobedience.

His saying: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together﴾, i.e., fight all of the polytheists together just as they fight all of you.

His saying: ﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous﴾, meaning, from wronging (zulm) through victory and triumph.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 37:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the postponement (al-nasi') is an increase in disbelief﴾. It has been recited without the hamza, but the well-known reading is with the hamza. The scholars of Arabic said: this is the more correct (reading), and al-nasi' means postponement; it is said, "Allah postponed (nasa'a) your term (ajal)," meaning: He delayed it.

The occasion of the revelation of the verse: the people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) used to make the sacred month (al-muharram) permissible at one time and forbidden at another. When they made the sacred month permissible, they substituted Safar for it in its prohibition. The reason for this was that most of their livelihood came from raids, fighting and swords, so it was hard for them to refrain from fighting for three consecutive months. The one who undertook the making lawful and unlawful (of months) was a man from the Banu Kinanah called Abu Thumamah, who inherited it from his forefathers. He would stand upon a camel and say: "O people, I am not blamed, I am not contradicted, and my judgment is not rejected. Indeed, I have made the sacred month lawful this year and made Safar forbidden." A man from among them said: "Are we not the postponers (al-nasi'un) for Mu'add? The months of lawfulness, he makes them forbidden." This is the meaning of al-nasi' mentioned in the verse.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿an increase in disbelief﴾ mean: an increase of disbelief upon their disbelief.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿by which those who disbelieved are led astray﴾, meaning: Allah leads astray by it those who disbelieved. It has been recited as "yuḍalla bihi alladhina kafaru" in the passive form (without naming the agent), and it has been recited as "yuḍilla bihi alladhina kafaru" (with Allah as agent), which is the better known, and it is the apparent meaning.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿they make it lawful one year and make it forbidden another year﴾. We have already mentioned the meaning. His words: ﴿so that they may agree (liyuwati'u)﴾ mean: so that they may agree (liyuwafiqu), and mu'atha'ah means agreement. Its meaning: so that they may agree with ﴿the number of what Allah has forbidden﴾, i.e., the count of what Allah has forbidden, ﴿and so make lawful what Allah has forbidden﴾, i.e., they say: four and four. His words: ﴿Their evil deeds have been made attractive to them, and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ — the meaning is apparent.

There is another opinion regarding the verse: that al-nasi' is the postponement of the Hajj by one month every year. They said: Abu Bakr performed Hajj in the year nine in Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed Hajj in the year ten in Dhu al-Hijjah, and this is the meaning of his saying: "Indeed, time has turned around to its original state," the report we have mentioned.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, what is [wrong] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth?﴾ This verse was revealed concerning the expedition of Tabuk. The expedition took place in the intense heat of summer, when the fruits had ripened and the shade was pleasant, so it was very difficult for the Muslims. Some of them stayed behind with an excuse, and some stayed behind without an excuse. So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse.

His saying: ﴿adhaqaltum ila al-ard﴾ (you adhere heavily to the earth), meaning: you were reluctant (tathaqaltum). The essential meaning is: you sat back from the raid and disliked going forth.

His saying: ﴿ila al-ard﴾ (to the earth), meaning: to this world (al-dunya). He called the world "earth" because it is on the earth.

His saying: ﴿Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter?﴾ meaning: are you satisfied with the pleasures of this world instead of the pleasures of the Hereafter.

His saying: ﴿Then the enjoyment of the life of this world, compared to the Hereafter, is but little.﴾ It is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: "All of the world is a small gathering compared to the gathering of the Hereafter." And it is authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The likeness of this world compared to the Hereafter is nothing but the likeness of one of you dipping his finger into the sea; let him see what it returns with."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 39:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ This is a threat and a warning for those who abandon going forth (nafr) in the way of Allah. Al-nafr (going forth) is the opposite of al-hudu' (rest) and al-sukun (stillness).

His words: ﴿and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all﴾ Its meaning: if harm (ḍarr) occurs, it returns to you, not to Him. ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾ its meaning is apparent.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿If you do not support him, then Allah has already supported him﴾. Its meaning: if you do not support him, Allah has supported him. ﴿When those who disbelieved drove him out﴾. We have already explained the account of their expulsion of him in His words: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾, [to the end of] the verse. His words ﴿the second of two﴾ mean: one of two. The Arabs say "khamis khamsa" (the fifth of five), meaning one of the five, and "rabi' arba'a" (the fourth of four), meaning one of the four.

The commentators (al-Mufassirun) said: Allah rebuked all people for abandoning the support of the Messenger, except Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. It was also said: "Support him" is addressed to my creation, except Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, for he did support him.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿when they were both in the cave﴾. The cave (al-ghar) is a hole in a mountain, and this mountain is Mount Thawr, a mountain near Makkah.

﴿When they were both in the cave, when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." So Allah sent down His tranquility (sakinah) upon him and strengthened him﴾.

His words ﴿when he said to his companion﴾ mean: to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, by the consensus of the scholars.

It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Abu Bakr is my companion in the cave, and my companion at the Pool (al-hawd)."

It is narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Bajali that he said: Whoever says that Abu Bakr is not the companion of the Messenger of Allah is a disbeliever, because he denies the explicit text of the Qur'an. As for the rest of the Companions, if one denies their companionship, he is an innovator (mubtadi') and not a disbeliever.

His words ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾. It is narrated that when the Prophet (ﷺ) left with Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, he commanded Ali to lie down on his bed, and told him that no harm would befall him. He went out with Abu Bakr before the cave. The polytheists came seeking the Prophet (ﷺ), and Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, rose from his bed. They said to him, "Where is your companion?" He said, "I do not know." So they set out in pursuit, following his tracks, until they reached the cave. When Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, sensed them, he became very frightened and said, "O Messenger of Allah, if I am killed, one person perishes; but if you are killed, this entire nation perishes." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." It is also established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O Abu Bakr! What do you think of two whom Allah is the third of?" In the account it is also said that Allah caused an acacia-like shrub (thumamah) to grow at the mouth of the cave, a small tree, and inspired a dove to lay eggs until they hatched, and inspired a spider to spin its web.

His words, the Exalted: ﴿So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions. The first: upon the Prophet. This is the preference of al-Zajjaj. The second: that it was upon Abu Bakr. This is the view of the majority, because sakinah here means that by which the heart is calmed, and Abu Bakr was the one who was afraid and grieved, not the Messenger of Allah.

There is a third opinion regarding the verse: that the sakinah was sent down upon both of them. It is transmitted in the codex of Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with her: "So Allah sent down His tranquility upon both of them, and strengthened both of them with armies you did not see." His words ﴿and strengthened him with armies you did not see﴾: the armies here are the angels, who descended and cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers until they turned back. His words ﴿and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest﴾: their word is shirk, and it is the lowest until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And the word of Allah is the highest﴾, meaning: there is no god but Allah, and it is the highest until the Day of Resurrection. His words ﴿And Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise﴾: we have already explained the meanings of al-'Aziz (the Exalted in Might) and al-Hakim (the Wise).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 41:

His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy⁠﻿﻿ ﻿﻿﻿—﻿﻿ it is said that this verse is the first verse to be revealed from Surat al-Tawba.

As for His statement ﴿light or heavy⁠﻿﻿﻿—﻿﻿﻿﻿ there are several opinions. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada that they both said: "Eager and not eager." Al-Azhari said: "Nashat (eager) is the plural of nashit."

The second opinion is that of al-Hasan al-Basri: "Go forth in ease and hardship." This is a good opinion. It is also narrated from al-Hakam ibn ʿUtayba: "Occupied and not occupied." It is narrated from Abu Talha, a companion of the Prophet: "Elderly and young." There is a fifth opinion: "On foot and on horseback." ﴿And strive with your wealth and your lives in the way of Allah...﴾ up to the end of the verse. Its meaning is clear. It was also said: this verse is abrogated by His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾ up to the end of the verse. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 42:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had it been a near gain and a moderate journey, they would have followed you.﴾ That is: had it been a gain near at hand and easy to obtain. ﴿And a moderate journey﴾ means a short, easy journey [near]. ﴿They would have followed you.﴾ That is: they would have gone out with you. ﴿But the distance seemed long to them.﴾ That is: the journey seemed long to them. Al-shuqqah (the distance, hardship of travel) in the language is the goal that one intends to reach.

His saying: ﴿And they will swear by Allah, "Had we been able, we would have gone out with you."﴾ This refers to the hypocrites.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They destroy themselves﴾ means: by the false oath. His saying: ﴿And Allah knows that they are liars﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 43:

His words, the Exalted: ﴿May Allah pardon you. Why did you grant them permission?﴾ It is related from Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi that he said: The Messenger of Allah did two things without permission from Allah: he ransomed the captives of Badr, and he granted permission to those who stayed behind in the expedition of Tabuk. Allah, the Exalted, rebuked him for both of them. In the placing of His words ﴿May Allah pardon you﴾ at the beginning there is a subtle meaning in safeguarding the heart of the Prophet.

His words: ﴿Until it becomes clear to you who are truthful and you know the liars﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission﴾. Its meaning: they do not ask your permission to stay behind (al-takhalluf).

As for His saying ﴿that they strive with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah﴾, and the rest of the verse, it is well known. Then he said:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 45:

: ﴿Only those seek your permission who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, and whose hearts are in doubt﴾, that is: their hearts are in doubt. ﴿So in their doubt they hesitate back and forth﴾, that is: they are bewildered.

Then he said:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 46:

﴿And had they intended to go out, they would have made preparation for it, some provision.﴾ It means: if they had intended to go out, they would have made preparation for it, some provision, that is, the equipment of travel: provisions, a mount, and other things. ﴿But Allah disliked their departure, so He held them back.﴾ Its meaning: their going forth. ﴿So He discouraged them﴾ means: He made them lazy and restrained them from going out. ﴿And it was said, "Sit with those who sit."﴾ Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "It was inspired into their hearts." Others said: some of them said to others, "Sit with those who sit."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 47:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Had they gone out with you, they would have added nothing to you but corruption﴾. This verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk. The meaning of His words ﴿khabalan﴾ is: corruption and evil. The meaning of corruption is: sowing cowardice and weakness among the believers.

As for His words ﴿wa-la-awdaʿu khilalakum﴾: al-iyda' (hastening, quick pace) is swift travel. The rajaz poet said:

(Would that I were in it as a young camel, who runs swiftly in it and hastens)

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of the verse is: "They would have hastened among you with what causes discord among you." Others said: "They would have hastened among you by sowing hatred and enmity through tale-bearing, and by carrying speech from one to another." Upon this view, His words ﴿khilalakum﴾ mean: among you (lit. your midst). ﴿yabghunakumu al-fitnah﴾ means: they seek discord for you. The word fitnah has two meanings: one is polytheism (shirk), and the other is the division of the word (i.e., the unity of the community).

﴿wa-fikum sammaʿunalahum﴾: concerning this there are two views:

The first: among you are spies for them who carry speech to them. Ibn ʿUyaynah was asked: "Is there mention of spies in the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes," and he cited this verse.

The second view: ﴿wa-fikum sammaʿunalahum﴾ means: among you are those who listen to them, i.e., accept what they say. From this is what is related concerning the prayer: "Allah hears whoever praises Him" (sami‘a Allahu liman hamidah), meaning: Allah accepts whoever praises Him. And from Abu ʿUbaydah: "wa-fikum sammaʿunalahum": obedient to them. The meaning is close to the second view.

﴿wa-Allahu ʿalimun bi-l-zalimin﴾: its meaning is that He knows them. If one says: He said at the beginning of the verse, ﴿they would have added nothing to you but corruption﴾, and the Prophet and his companions were not in corruption, so how could they add to it?

The answer: the meaning of the verse is: they would have added no strength to you; rather, they would have sought corruption for you.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, they had sought discord before, and they had turned matters over against you﴾ — the verse. Ibtigha' (seeking) means seeking out, and fitna (discord) means bringing about dissension that leads to the splitting of the word (unity). His saying ﴿and they had turned matters over against you﴾ means: they reversed matters for you and wanted them turned upside down and inside out. The real meaning is that they sought by every means to corrupt your affair, ﴿until the truth came and the command of Allah became manifest, while they were averse﴾ — its meaning is well known."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 49:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not put me to trial."﴾ Most of the exegetes say that this verse was revealed concerning a hypocrite man called al-Jadd ibn Qays. The Messenger of Allah said to him: "Would you like to go to the battle against the sons of al-Asfar (meaning the Romans)? Perhaps you might obtain some captive women from them." The Messenger of Allah urged him to set out, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, grant me leave" (meaning: to stay behind), "and do not put me to trial" (meaning: with the women of the Romans). He said: "My people know that I am greatly taken with women," meaning: infatuated.

This is one of the two views concerning His words: ﴿and do not put me to trial﴾.

The second view is that its meaning is: "Do not make me sinful." Qatadah said: its meaning is, "Do not tempt me to set out, for going out is difficult for me, so I would stay behind and fall into sin."

As for His words: ﴿Surely, into trial they have already fallen﴾, there are two meanings to it:

One of them: Surely, into Hell they have fallen. The other: Surely, into polytheism they have fallen.

﴿And indeed, Hell is encompassing of the disbelievers﴾, surrounding the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 50:

The words of the Most High: ﴿If good befalls you, it distresses them﴾. The "good" (al-hasanah) here is the blessing by which a person's soul is made content and his life made pleasant. In other places, al-hasanah means obedience (ta'ah).

﴿And if misfortune befalls you﴾. The "misfortune" (al-musibah) here is the affliction in fighting, by the Muslims being struck by the disbelievers. It is said: the good mentioned was on the day of Badr, and the misfortune mentioned was on the day of Uhud.

And His saying: ﴿They say, "We had already taken our precaution beforehand"﴾, meaning: we were cautious beforehand. Its meaning is: we guarded ourselves against falling into misfortune. ﴿And they turn away while they are rejoicing﴾, its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Nothing will ever afflict us except what Allah has decreed for us.﴾ Allah, exalted is He, commanded the believers to answer them with this.

And His saying: ﴿except what Allah has decreed for us﴾ means: upon us. It was also said that its meaning is: what Allah has informed us of. ﴿He is our Protector, and upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ He is our Guardian and our Helper, and upon Him the believers depend. In the well-known report transmitted through Abu al-Darda', the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A servant does not reach the reality of faith (haqiqat al-iman) until he knows that what has befallen him would not have missed him, and that what has missed him would not have befallen him."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 52:

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Say: "Do you await for us [anything] except one of the two best outcomes?"﴾ — "Do you await for us" means: do you wait for us? ﴿except one of the two best outcomes﴾. The dual of al-husna (the best) is al-husnayan (the two best outcomes): one of them is victory, and the other is martyrdom.

Abu Hurayra narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah guarantees for whoever goes out in His cause, out of faith and seeking reward, that He will admit him into Paradise, or return him to his dwelling from which he set out, along with the reward or spoils he has gained."

And His statement: ﴿And we await for you﴾ — meaning: we wait for you — ﴿that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him, or at our hands﴾. The punishment from Him is the calamity that descends from the sky, and the punishment at the hands of the believers is the punishment by the sword. ﴿So wait; indeed we are waiting with you﴾ — so wait, for indeed we are waiting along with you.

Almighty God says: ﴿Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will never be accepted from you.﴾ This is a command with the meaning of a condition, and its meaning is: if you spend, willingly or unwillingly, ﴿it will never be accepted from you, for you have indeed been a deviant people (qawman fasiqin).﴾ That is because you have been a deviant people, and fisq (deviance, transgression) here means kufr (disbelief).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 54:

The words of God the Exalted: ﴿And nothing prevents their contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in God and His Messenger﴾. Its meaning is: the thing that prevents their contributions from being accepted is their disbelief in God and His Messenger.

And His words: ﴿And they do not come to the prayer except while they are lazy﴾, meaning: burdened and reluctant. If it is said: how does He mention laziness in prayer when there is no prayer at all?

We say: the censure falls upon the disbelief that prompts laziness, for disbelief makes one lazy, while faith energizes. It is said: the root of every disbelief is laziness. And there is the proverb: laziness is sweeter than honey. ﴿And they do not spend except while they are unwilling﴾, whose meaning is clear. The real meaning in all of this is: they do not pray, nor do they spend, except out of fear; as for drawing near to God, there is none.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 55:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you.﴾ Ijab (admiration) for a thing is delight in it.

And His saying: ﴿Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the worldly life.﴾ Here there is a question, namely it is said: How can punishment come through wealth and children when they are enjoying their wealth and children?

The answer has several aspects:

The first: that in the verse there is taqdim and ta'khir (inversion of order), as if the Exalted had said: "So let not their wealth nor their children impress you in the worldly life; Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the Hereafter."

The second view: the punishment is the calamities that befall their wealth and children.

The third: the meaning of punishment is the toil in gathering (wealth), the preoccupation of the heart with guarding it, the reluctance to spend while spending, their being made to swear oaths before those who do not praise them, and their coming before those who do not act justly.

And His saying: ﴿and their souls depart while they are disbelievers﴾ means their souls depart while they are disbelievers.

In the verse there is a refutation of the Qadariyya, and it is evident.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 56:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they swear by Allah that they are surely of you﴾, meaning: of your number. ﴿But they are not of you﴾, meaning: they are not of your number. ﴿Rather, they are a people who are fearful﴾, that is: they are afraid.

In the accounts (al-hikayat) it is related that a certain heretic (mulhid) was seen performing a fine prayer, and when he was asked about this he said: "It is the custom of the people of the land, and the preservation of wealth and children."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 57:

The Most High said: ﴿If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a place to enter﴾. Qatadah said: "The refuge (al-multaja') is the fortresses (al-husun), the caves (al-maghharat) are the ravines (al-ghiran), and the place to enter (al-madkhal) is the burrows (al-asrab)." This is a good opinion. The meaning of the verse is: if they could find a means of escape from you and a place to flee to, they would certainly leave you. This is the meaning of the Most High's words: ﴿they would turn away to it while they rush headlong﴾, meaning: they would hasten. It is said: "a horse is jammah (jamuh) when nothing turns it back from its direction."

The poet said:

(You have charged headlong, charging through their blood, until you saw the nobles of them fallen still.)

It is related from Anas that he recited: "wa hum yajmarun" (and they are hurrying), and the meaning is close to the first reading.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on Surah 9, verse 58:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And among them are those who find fault with you concerning the charities﴾. That is, they criticize you regarding the distribution of the charities. It is said: al-hamz and al-lamz have the same meaning. It is also said: al-lumaza is one who criticizes people with his speech, and al-hamaza is one who gestures with his eye [mockery].

The occasion of revelation (sabab nuzul) of the verse: Dhu al-Khuwaysira al-Tamimi, whose name was Harqus ibn Zuhayr, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was distributing, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, be just!" He said: "Who will be just if I am not just?" Then he said: "There will come forth from the progeny of this man people who will regard your prayer as insignificant compared to their prayer, and your fasting as insignificant compared to their fasting. They will pass through the religion as an arrow passes through its target." The report continues, and then Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿If they are given from them, they are pleased, but if they are not given from them, behold, they become angry﴾. This was said about Tha'laba ibn Hatib and his companions. They would be pleased if they were given much, but if they were given little, they would become angry and find fault.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 59:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them, and had said, "Allah is sufficient for us (kafina Allah)! Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. Indeed, to Allah we turn in hope (inna ila Allah raghibun)."﴾ That is: if only they had been content with what you (Muhammad) did. ﴿Zakat is only for the poor and the needy, and for those employed to collect it, and for those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and for freeing captives...﴾ And had they desired more, it would have been better for them than their anger and their faultfinding.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 60:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾ — the verse. The faqir (poor) linguistically is the one in need whose need has broken his back; and the miskin (needy) is the one whose soul has been weakened from moving in the pursuit of strength, so it has become still. As for the discussion, there are many opinions regarding the faqir and the miskin in the verse.

The first: it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid and al-Zuhri that they said: the faqir is the one who does not ask. Some of them said otherwise.

The second: the view of Qatadah, namely that the faqir is one who has a disability and has nothing, and the miskin is one who has nothing but has no disability. Some of them said in accordance with what Qatadah said.

The third: that the fuqara' are the Muhajirun (emigrants), and the masakin are the A'rab (Bedouins). This is the view of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i.

The fourth: that the fuqara' are the needy Muslims, and the masakin are the needy among the People of the Covenant (dhimmis).

There is a fifth view: that the faqir and the miskin are one and the same. They differ as to which of the two is in greater need. The madhhab of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, is that the faqir is in greater need than the miskin, and he cited His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As for the boat, it belonged to the masakin﴾, so He called them masakin although they had a boat. Al-Asma'i and a group of the people of language claimed that the miskin is in greater need than the faqir, and they recited:

(As for the faqir whose milch-camel... was enough for his dependents, yet nothing of him [remained]...)

Yunus al-Nahwi said: I said to a Bedouin, "Are you a faqir?" He said, "No, a miskin" — meaning: lower than the faqir.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and the workers upon them﴾ — meaning: the collectors (of zakat), and they have a known share of the alms.

And it is narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As that they receive an amount equal to the standard wage (ajr al-mithl).

As for His saying: ﴿and those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾, the people of knowledge said: those whose hearts are to be reconciled are of two kinds: Muslims and polytheists, and each kind is of two sorts. As for the Muslims: a people whose faith was weak, such as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, 'Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari, al-Aqra' ibn Habis, 'Abbas ibn Mirdas and their like; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to give them so that they would be reconciled to faith and their faith would be strengthened. And a kind whose faith was strong, such as 'Adi ibn Hatim, al-Zibriqan ibn Badr and others; he used to give them so that their tribe would be reconciled.

As for the polytheists, they are of two kinds: a kind he would give to repel their harm from the Muslims, such as 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl and others; and a kind he would give so that they would believe and incline towards him, such as Safwan ibn Umayya ibn Khalaf and Malik ibn 'Awf al-Nasri and others.

They differed as to whether the share of those whose hearts are to be reconciled remains after the Prophet (ﷺ)?
