Al-Sha'bi and a group said: it has lapsed. This is the view of most of the people of knowledge. Al-Zuhri said: it remains. Both opinions have been reported from al-Shafi'i, and the sound one is the first.

His saying: ﴿and for the captives (ar-riqab)﴾ — concerning it there are two views:

The first: that they are the mukatabun (slaves contracted to buy their freedom). This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa and others.

Malik said: that share is used to buy slaves who are then freed. The sound view is the first.

His saying: ﴿and the debtors﴾ — Mujahid said: these are people whose homes were burned by fire, and whose wealth was swept away by a flood, so they incurred debts for their expenses. Others said: it is everyone who incurs debt for a reason in which there is no sin.

His saying: ﴿and in the way of Allah﴾ — these are the warriors (ghuzat) and the pilgrims (hujjaj). His saying: ﴿in the way of Allah﴾ means: in obedience to Allah. ﴿And the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil)﴾ — concerning it there are two views:

The first: that he is one whose road was cut off, so he remained poor with no wealth. The view upon which the jurists agree is that he is one who has been separated from his wealth; so a share of the alms is given to him even if he is rich in his own land.

Ibn al-Anbari related a third view: that ibn al-sabil is the guest.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿an obligation from Allah﴾ — meaning: Allah has enjoined this as an obligation. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ — All-Knowing of what benefits His creation, All-Wise in what He has arranged.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 61:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, "He is an ear."﴾ The word "ear" (udhun) here means one who hears everything that is said to him. The poet said:

(O heart, be distracted with Baddan... indeed my concern is with listening and with the ear.)

The occasion of the revelation of the verse: the hypocrites said, "Say whatever you wish, then deny it and swear oaths, for Muhammad is an ear; he hears everything that is said to him and accepts it."

﴿Say, "An ear of goodness for you."﴾ That is: this quality is good for you. It is as if he said: a listener who is good is good for you, and a listener who is evil is evil for you. ﴿He believes in Allah﴾ he affirms Allah, ﴿and believes the believers﴾ and affirms the believers. ﴿And a mercy for those of you who believe. And those who harm the Messenger of Allah, for them is a painful punishment.﴾ Its meaning is apparent. It was also read: "udhunun khayrun lakum" (an ear of goodness for you), meaning: more beneficial for you.

﴿They swear by Allah to you, to please you, but Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers.﴾ Its meaning is clear.

And His saying: ﴿if they are believers﴾. It was said: it means: they are not believers.

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger...﴾ (yuhadid Allah): meaning, whoever is on one side and in a boundary (hadd) apart from Allah and His Messenger. ﴿...then indeed for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein. That is the great disgrace.﴾ (al-khizy al-'azim): the great exposure (fadihah) and the great punishment (nakal).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 64:

His words, may Allah exalt him: ﴿The hypocrites fear﴾ (yahdharu al-munafiqun). There are two opinions regarding this:

The first: it is a report that carries the meaning of a command, and its meaning is: let the hypocrites be wary.

The second: it means a report about them, since they used to mock and feared exposure through the revelation of the Qur'an concerning them.

His words, may Allah exalt him: ﴿Lest there be sent down upon them a surah informing them of what is in their hearts﴾. We have already explained that this surah is called al-Muba'thirah (the one that uncovers) and al-Fadihah (the one that exposes); this verse alludes to what we mentioned earlier.

It has been related from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: Allah, exalted is He, revealed the mention of seventy men of the hypocrites by their names, their fathers' names, and their tribes. Then the mention of the names was abrogated (nasakha) out of mercy and compassion toward the believers, because their children were believers; so that was abrogated lest some of them reproach others.

His words, may Allah exalt him: ﴿Say: Mock on; surely Allah will bring forth what you fear﴾. Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 65:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And if you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing."﴾

The occasion of the revelation of the verse: "The Prophet was traveling on the expedition of Tabuk, and ahead of him were three of the hypocrites: two of them were mocking, and the third was laughing." It has also been said: their mockery was that they used to say, "Muhammad claims that he will overcome the Romans and conquer their cities. How far-fetched that is!"

It has also been said: they used to say, "Muhammad claims that the Qur'an was revealed concerning our companions who remained in Madinah, but it is merely his own saying and speech." This is the meaning of the verse. It is related that the Prophet sent to them: "What were you saying?" They replied: "We were only conversing about what the riders converse about." Then God the Most High said: ﴿Say, "Was it God, His signs, and His Messenger that you were mocking?"﴾

It is related from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "I saw Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul running ahead of the Prophet while stones were striking him, and he was saying, 'We were only conversing and playing'; and the Messenger of Allah was saying: ﴿Was it God, His signs, and His Messenger that you were mocking?﴾"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 66:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Do not make excuses; you have disbelieved after your belief.﴾ If someone says: "You have disbelieved after your belief," but they were not believers.

The answer to this: its meaning is that you displayed disbelief after you had displayed belief.

And the Exalted's saying: ﴿If We pardon a group among you﴾ — it has been recited as "naʿfu" (with the vowel on the nūn) and "yaʿfu"? Its two readings have one meaning. The "group" here is one man who was called Makhshī ibn Ḥumayr. He was the one who would laugh and would not join in the discussion with them. It is narrated that he separated himself from them, and so [God said]: ﴿If We pardon a group among you﴾, meaning this one individual, ﴿We will punish a group, because they were criminals.﴾ Its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 67:

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are of one another﴾ – the verse. His words: ﴿of one another﴾ have two explanations:

The first: some of them are upon the religion of others.

The second: their affair is one and the same. This is like a man saying to another: "I am from you," meaning: my affair and your affair are one.

﴿They enjoin what is evil﴾ has two explanations:

The first: the evil (munkar) is shirk, and the good (ma'ruf) is faith in Allah.

It is related from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi that he said: everything mentioned as munkar in the Qur'an is the worship of idols and association of partners with Allah.

The second explanation: the munkar is disobedience to Allah, and the ma'ruf is obedience to Allah.

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿and they forbid what is good﴾. The more apparent meaning of His words ﴿and they withhold their hands﴾ is that they withhold from spending in the way of Allah.

The second explanation: "they withhold their hands" means they refrain from jihad in the way of Allah.

Some of the later scholars said: it means they do not extend their hands in supplication and in longing toward Allah.

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾, that is: they abandoned the command of Allah, so He abandoned them from His mercy. It is narrated from Qatadah that he said: they forgot the good and did not forget the evil.

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: they are those who step outside the obedience of Allah.

It is authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he is entrusted he betrays, and when he promises he breaks it (fails)." In some narrations: "when he makes a covenant he betrays it." In some reports: "They do not come to the prayer except lazily, and they do not recite the Qur'an except briefly." In some narrations from Ibn 'Abbas: the number of hypocrite men in the time of the Messenger of Allah was three hundred, and the number of women was one hundred and seventy.

Almost all of the passage is commentary; the Qur'anic quotations are marked with ﴿ ﴾ and will be rendered as their meaning within those markers.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding therein﴾ is well known. And His saying: ﴿It is sufficient for them﴾ means: sufficient for them. ﴿And Allah has cursed them﴾ means: Allah has removed them far from His mercy. ﴿And for them is an enduring punishment﴾ means: lasting.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 69:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Like those before you﴾ means: you, O assembly of the hypocrites, are like those before you. His saying: ﴿They were greater than you in strength and more abundant in wealth and children, so they enjoyed their portion (khalaq)﴾. The khalaq (portion, share) is the allotted share; it was also said it is the abundant good fortune. The meaning of the verse: they enjoyed by following their desires, ﴿as you enjoyed your portion﴾ by following your desires. It was also said: the meaning of the verse is that they were content with their share of the worldly life in exchange for their share of the Hereafter. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And you engaged in vain talk as they engaged in vain talk﴾ means: they played and mocked, just as you did. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the losers﴾ means: just as their deeds became worthless and they lost, so too your deeds have become worthless and you have lost. It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "You will certainly follow the ways of those before you, to the extent that if one of them had entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it too." And from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "How much the present night resembles the past one, in this world and the Hereafter."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 70:

His the Exalted's saying: ﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them﴾, meaning: the report of those before them, ﴿the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Ibrahim, and the companions of Madyan﴾. Madyan is the name of the town of Shuʿayb. His saying: ﴿and the overturned cities﴾ refers to the towns of Lut; they were named "overturned" (mu'tafikah) because Allah the Exalted overturned them with their people.

His saying: ﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning with arguments. ﴿And Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves﴾. Its meaning: Allah did not diminish their share, but they diminished their own share and harmed themselves.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 9, verse 71:

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the believing men and the believing women are allies of one another﴾. This alliance (wilaya) is the alliance of religion and unity of word. It is also said concerning the interpretation of the verse: the Emigrants (Muhajirun) and the Helpers (Ansar) are allies of one another, and the Freed Captives (Tulaqa') of Quraysh and the Manumitted Slaves (Utaqa') of Thaqif are allies of one another.

The words of God Most High: ﴿They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they establish prayer and give zakah﴾, to the end of the verse, its meaning is well known. As for His words: ﴿And they obey God and His Messenger. Those — God will have mercy upon them﴾, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ said: it is following the Book and the Sunnah. As for His words: ﴿Indeed, God is Almighty and Wise﴾, that is: Almighty in His help, Wise in His management.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 72:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein﴾. "Gardens" (jannat): orchards. ﴿Beneath which rivers flow﴾: these are the rivers that Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned in Surat Muhammad.

His saying: ﴿and pleasant dwellings﴾. It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Abbas that he said: ﴿and pleasant dwellings﴾ is a palace of pearls, in which there are seventy houses of chrysolite (zabarjad), in each house seventy chambers of ruby (yaqut), in each chamber seventy beds, on each bed seventy couches of every color, on each couch a wife from the dark-eyed houris (al-hur al-'in).

Also in the reports (al-athar), concerning His saying ﴿in gardens of Eden﴾, it is said that the Garden of Eden is the abode of the prophets, the truthful (siddiqin) and the martyrs, and all the other gardens surround it. It is also said: the Garden of Eden is in the seventh heaven, and none enters it except a prophet, a truthful one, a just leader, or a man who has been tested (muhakkam) in himself. The meaning of "tested in himself" is: he was given the choice between disbelief and being killed, so he chose being killed. As for the Garden of Refuge (jannat al-ma'wa), it is in the lowest heaven.

His saying ﴿'adn﴾ means a place of residence. It is said: 'adana bi-l-makan when he resided in the place. The poet said:

(If you seek hospitality from his forbearance... you will be hosted by a noble one who has settled there.)

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and approval from Allah is greater﴾: its meaning is that Allah's pleasure is greater than these gifts.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Exalted is He, says: O people of Paradise! They say: Here we are, our Lord, at Your service and pleasure, and the good is in Your hands. He says: Are you pleased with Me? They say: And why would we not be pleased, when You have given us what You have not given any of Your creation? He says: And I will give you better than that. They say: And what is better than that? He says: I will cause My pleasure (ridwan) to descend upon you (ahill, i.e., anzal, "cause to descend"), so I shall never be angry with you again." Al-Bukhari and Muslim recorded it in their two Sahihs.

His saying ﴿That is the great triumph﴾: its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 73:

﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them.﴾ The people of tafsir (tafsir, exegesis) said: its meaning is: strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and against the hypocrites with the tongue. It is related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Do not meet the hypocrite except with a scowling face." It is also related from him that he said: "One should strive with his hand; if he is not able, then with his tongue; if he is not able, then with his heart." As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿and be harsh with them﴾, the ghilzah (harshness, sternness) here is: severe rebuke (intihar, harsh reprimand). His words: ﴿Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Allah's words: ﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say [it], but they did say the word of disbelief﴾, and so on. This verse was also revealed concerning the hypocrites (al-munafiqun). Scholars differed over what "the word of disbelief" refers to.

Some said: the word of disbelief is cursing Muhammad (ﷺ). Others said: the word of disbelief is the statement of al-Jallas ibn Suwayd, for he said: "If what Muhammad says is true, then we are worse than donkeys."

﴿And they disbelieved after their Islam, and they plotted what they could not attain, and they resented only that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty. So if they repent, it will be better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world﴾. There is a third view: the word of disbelief is their saying, "If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it." By "the mightier" they meant Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and they said: "We will set out with the crown, in opposition to Muhammad."

As for Allah's words, ﴿And they disbelieved after their Islam﴾, its meaning is: they openly showed disbelief after openly showing Islam.

As for His words, ﴿and they plotted what they could not attain﴾, it means: they aimed at what they could not achieve. It is narrated that twelve hypocrites gathered during the expedition of Tabuk (ghazwa, a military campaign led by the Prophet) to assassinate the Prophet. It is also narrated that they intended to push him down from the 'Aqabah into the valley, but Allah repelled their evil from the Prophet. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿and they plotted what they could not attain﴾.

As for His words, ﴿and they resented only that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty﴾, "resented" means "disliked." A poet, praising the Banu Umayyah, said:

"They resented nothing in the Banu Umayyah
except that they are forbearing when they are angry.
And they are the masters of kings,
and none is fit to rule the Arabs but them."

As for His words, ﴿except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty﴾, it means: through the spoils of war. It is narrated that al-Jallas ibn Suwayd had taken on a debt (hamalah, a sum undertaken to settle a dispute or blood-money), and the Messenger of Allah paid it on his behalf. It is also narrated that Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had been owed blood-money by a people, and the Prophet ordered that it be paid to him in full. All of this is the meaning of His words: ﴿except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty﴾.

As for His words, ﴿So if they repent, it will be better for them﴾, it is narrated that when this verse was revealed, al-Jallas ibn Suwayd said: "I see that Allah is offering me repentance, and I have repented to Allah from what I was in." It is narrated that his faith was then found to be sound, and he was martyred on the Day of Yamamah.

As for His words, ﴿But if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no protector or helper in the earth﴾, to the end of the verse, its meaning is clear.

It is said regarding His words, ﴿and they resented only that Allah had enriched them﴾, that it means: they have no dislike or resentment at all. This is like the saying of the poet:

"And there is no fault in us, except that our swords
are notched from the clashing of the battalions."

That is, there is no fault in us at all.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verses 75–76:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with God: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous."﴾ That is: "we will surely give charity" (La-natasaddaqanna). The letter tā' (ت) was assimilated into ṣād (ص) and doubled (shuddiddat), meaning: "we will surely give charity in the ways of good, such as jihad and other things, and we will surely be among the righteous." It has been said that they were like ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and others in giving and bestowing.

Regarding the verse there are two opinions. The first: it was revealed concerning a man from the Anṣār who had property that was far away, and he said: "If God returns my property to me, I will certainly do such-and-such," and God returned his property to him, but he did nothing, so God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse concerning him.

The second opinion: it was revealed concerning Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib. Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī narrated: "Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of God, invoke God to grant me wealth.' He said: 'A little that suffices you is better than much that you cannot fulfil its due.' He said: 'O Messenger of God, invoke God to grant me wealth.' He said: 'Are you not content to be like the Messenger of God? By God, if you wished the mountains to travel with me as gold and silver, they would travel.' He said: 'O Messenger of God, invoke God to grant me wealth. By God, if You grant me wealth, I will surely give every person who has a right his right.' So the Messenger of God invoked God and said: 'O God, grant Thaʿlabah wealth.' He said: 'So he acquired sheep, and they multiplied as worms multiply, until the alleys of Medina became too narrow for them, so he went out with them to the desert, and he began to attend the five prayers, then they multiplied until the pastures of Medina became too narrow for them, so he moved further away, and he began to attend only the Friday prayer, then he abandoned attending the prayers and the Friday prayer altogether.' He said: 'So the Messenger of God sent his collector (muṣaddiq) to take the zakāt, and he passed by him and asked him for the zakāt. He said: "I see this as nothing but a sister of the jizyah. Go away until you come back to me." When he returned to him, he gave him nothing and said: "Until I meet the Messenger of God." So the collector returned and informed the Prophet of his matter, and God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse.' It was narrated that it was mentioned to him that this verse had been revealed concerning him, so he came to Medina and said: 'O Messenger of God, take my zakāt from me,' but he refused to take it. When the Messenger of God passed away, he came to Abū Bakr and asked him to take his zakāt, and he said: 'The Messenger of God did not take it, so I will not take it either.' And it was the same in the time of ʿUmar and the time of ʿUthmān, and he died in the time of ʿUthmān."

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with God: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous."﴾ That is: "we will surely give charity" (La-natasaddaqanna). Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 77:

The Most High's saying: ﴿So He caused hypocrisy to follow them into their hearts﴾ has two meanings.

The first: He repaid them with hypocrisy in their hearts. It is said: a'qabahu and 'aqabahu have the same meaning.

The second meaning: He made hypocrisy in their hearts a successor (to their broken promise), i.e., He left them with hypocrisy in their hearts.

﴿Until the Day they meet Him﴾: the Day of Resurrection.

The Most High's saying: ﴿because they broke their promise to Allah in what they had promised Him, and because they used to lie﴾.

Then He said: ﴿Did they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private counsel?﴾ Meaning: what they concealed in their hearts and what they confided to one another in secret. ﴿And that Allah is the Knower of the unseen matters﴾. Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 79:

The words of God the Exalted: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give charity voluntarily, and with those who find nothing to give except their effort⟩. Yalmizun (يَلْمِزُونَ): they criticize (يعيبون).

The occasion of revelation of the verse: "The Prophet urged the people to give charity. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came with four thousand dinars, which was half his wealth, and ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī came with three hundred wasq of dates (the wasq being a camel's load). Abū ʿAqīl, a man from the Anṣār, came with a ṣāʿ of dates and said: 'I had two ṣāʿ of dates, so I brought one of them.' The hypocrites said: 'As for ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī, they gave what they gave only for show. As for Abū ʿAqīl, God has no need of Abū ʿAqīl's ṣāʿ.' So God the Exalted revealed this verse concerning them."

﴿Al-muṭawwiʿīn⟩ (the volunteers) among the believers: this refers to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī. ﴿Wa-alladhīna lā yajidūna illā juhdahum⟩ (and those who find nothing but their effort): this refers to Abū ʿAqīl. Al-juhd: the capacity (al-ṭāqa). ﴿Fa-yaskharūna minhum⟩ (they mock them): they ridicule them. ﴿Sakhira Allāh minhum⟩ (God mocks them): He recompenses them with the recompense of mockery. ﴿Wa-lahum ʿadhābun alīm⟩ (and for them is a painful punishment).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 80:

His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them. Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them﴾, to the end of the verse. He intended by this the affirmation of despair of hope for their forgiveness.

It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that he related from the Prophet (ﷺ), in mursal form, that he said: "By Allah, I will surely add to the seventy." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them﴾. The mention of the number seventy was for emphasis in affirming despair. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾; its meaning is known.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 81:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced﴾. Al-farah (joy): a pleasure in the heart at attaining what is desired, and al-ghamm (grief): a constriction in the heart at the loss of what is desired. As for al-mukhallafun (those left behind), they are those who stayed back from the expedition (al-ghazw) and abandoned going out with the Messenger of Allah. Al-mukhallaf: the one who is left behind. His saying: ﴿by their sitting (maq'adihim)﴾ means: by their staying behind. His saying: ﴿against the Messenger of Allah (khilaf rasul Allah)﴾ has two meanings: the first: opposition to the Messenger of Allah. The second: by their sitting "khilaf" Messenger of Allah, i.e., after the Messenger of Allah, as said by Abu 'Ubaydah. ﴿And they disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah﴾. Jihad with wealth is spending (al-infaq), and jihad with the self is directly engaging in fighting (al-qital). His saying: ﴿and they disliked﴾ means: they did not love. ﴿And they said: Do not go forth in the heat﴾. Al-harr: is the blaze of the sun, and al-bard (cold) is its opposite. ﴿Say: The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat﴾ means: more intense in blaze. ﴿If only they understood﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "If only they knew (law kanu ya'lamun)." The meaning is one and the same.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on Surah 9, verse 82:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿So let them laugh a little and let them weep much﴾. Laughter (al-dahk) is a state that occurs in a person out of wonder or joy, while weeping (al-buka') is a state that overtakes a person out of grief and constriction of the heart, together with tears flowing down the cheek. It is said that laughter among the children of Adam is like neighing among horses.

There are two views concerning the verse. The first: the meaning of His words ﴿So let them laugh a little﴾ is: in this world; ﴿and let them weep much﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿as a recompense for what they used to earn﴾. This was stated by Abu Razin, al-Hasan (al-Basri), and a group.

The second view: this is a command in the sense of a report, as if He had said: they will laugh a little and weep much, meaning in the Hereafter.

If someone says: How does He say "they will laugh a little" when they will not laugh at all in the Hereafter?

The answer: We say that the meaning of His words "they will laugh a little" is that they will not laugh at all. This is like His words, exalted is He: ﴿So little is it that they believe﴾, meaning: they do not believe at all.

It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: Indeed the people of the Fire will weep, and their tears will not dry up, until if ships were sent running through their tears, they would run.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 83:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So if Allah brings you back to a group of them, and they ask your permission to go out [to fight], then say: "You will never go out with me, nor will you fight an enemy with me."﴾ That is, if Allah returns you to a group of them, and they ask your permission to go out, so that they may go out with you to fight. ﴿Say: "You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me."﴾ The people of tafsir (tafsir: Qur'anic exegesis) said: "The enemy here" refers to the People of the Book, for no polytheist remained in the Arabian Peninsula at that time. His saying: ﴿Indeed, you were pleased with sitting [at home] the first time, so sit [now] with those who remain behind.﴾ Those who remain behind (al-khalifun) here are the women and the children. It was also said: they are the people with disabilities and the weak.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 84:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And never pray over any of them who has died, ever﴾ – the verse. This verse was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, for it has been narrated: "When death approached him, his son came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), asking him for his shirt so that he might shroud his father in it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him his shirt. In some narrations: he gave him the shirt that was over his own shirt, which was the outer one. [The son] refused and asked for the shirt that was next to his skin. When he died, [his son] came to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to pray over him, in accordance with his son's request and his will. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up to pray over him, ʿUmar took hold of his garment and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, will you pray over this hypocrite?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'My Lord has given me a choice,' and he recited the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾, and [he said]: 'I have chosen to pray over him.' He said: 'Then pray over him.' So Allah the Exalted revealed His words: ﴿And never pray over any of them who has died﴾."

In the narration of Anas: "When the Prophet stood to pray over him, Jibril (peace be upon him) took hold of the edge of his garment and prevented him from praying, so he gave up the prayer."

The first narration is in the Two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim).

As for His words: ﴿Nor stand at his grave﴾ – and in another narration: "The Prophet, whenever he prayed over a deceased person, would stand at his grave and supplicate." So Allah the Exalted forbade him from doing this with regard to the hypocrites.

If it is said: How is it permissible for the Prophet to pray over a hypocrite while he knows that he is a disbeliever in Allah?

The answer to this: he saw that as a matter of benefit. It has also been said, when he prayed over him: "Indeed my prayer over him will not avail him anything against the punishment of Allah."

In some narrations: when ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul asked him for his shirt, to seek blessing through it and to be shrouded in it, one thousand men of his people embraced Islam who had not previously embraced it, because of what they saw of the blessing [obtained] through the Prophet. [﴿Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and they died while they were defiantly disobedient﴾.] The rest of the verse is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let not their wealth or their children impress you﴾. We have already explained its meaning earlier. If it is said: what is the purpose of the repetition (al-takrar)?

The answer to this verse has two aspects. The first: it is for emphasis (al-ta'kid).

The second: the two verses were revealed concerning two groups of hypocrites (al-munafiqun), not one single group.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 86:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And when a surah is sent down, [saying], "Believe in Allah and strive alongside His Messenger,"﴾ — the meaning of the verse is clear.

And His words: ﴿The men of wealth among them ask your permission﴾ — al-tawl (ṭawl, abundance) is ampleness and wealth, by the consensus of the exegetes (mufassirun). It was said: the reason ampleness is called ṭawl is that a person shows superiority over people by it (yatatāwalu bihā al-nās).

And His words: ﴿And they say, "Leave us, that we may be with those who sit back."﴾ — meaning: with those who sit back from jihad.

Then He said: ﴿They were content to be with those who stay behind (al-khawalif)﴾. Qatada said: "al-khawalif" are the women. Others said: they are the lowly and base of the people. It is said: "So-and-so was left behind (khalifahu) by his people," when he was beneath them. His saying: ﴿And Allah has sealed upon their hearts, so they do not understand﴾. Taba' (sealed) means khatama (sealed up). It is also said: the tab'a (seal/stain) are black spots that fall upon the heart, by which the king (al-malik) recognizes the hypocrite from the believer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 88:

The words of the Most High: ﴿But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their selves﴾ — its meaning is well known.

And His words: ﴿And those, for them are the good things﴾ — concerning it there are several opinions:

One of them: that "the good things" (al-khayrat) are the spoils of war (al-ghana'im). The other: that "the good things" are the maidens (al-hur) in Paradise, and its singular is khayrah. The Most High said: ﴿therein are good, beautiful [women]﴾, meaning the maidens (al-hur).

The third opinion: that the meaning of "the good things" is known only to God. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas, and similar to this is the words of the Most High: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾.

﴿And those, they are the successful ones﴾ — the meaning has already been explained.
Then He said: ﴿Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾ Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 90:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who made excuses among the Bedouins came that they might be permitted [to stay behind]﴾. It has been recited in two ways: "al-mu'adhdhirun" and "al-mu'adhdhirun" [with the letters doubled differently]. Regarding al-mu'adhdhirin there are two opinions. The first: al-mu'adhdhirin are the al-mu'tadhirun (those who offer excuses), with the ta' assimilated into the dhal (idgham).

The second opinion: al-mu'adhdhirin are those who fall short (al-muqassirun), and ta'dhir in the language means taqsir (falling short, negligence). As for al-mu'adhdhirun, they are those who exaggerate in giving excuses. It is said in a proverb: "Indeed he has fully discharged the warning (la-qad a'dhara man andhar)," meaning: he went to the utmost in showing his excuse, the one who gave the warning beforehand. Labid said in verse:

(Until the year's end, then the greeting of peace upon you both... and whoever weeps a full year has made an excuse [exceeded in excuse].)

That is, he went to the utmost in excuse.

Know that this verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites, and they made excuses while they had no valid excuse. As for the Bedouins (al-a'rab), they are those who dwell in the desert, and the 'Arabi is the name for one who has Arab lineage.

His saying: ﴿And those who lied to Allah and His Messenger sat [at home]﴾. This is about the hypocrites; and the meaning of ﴿lied to Allah and His Messenger﴾ is that they did not bring a truthful excuse. Then He said: ﴿There will afflict those of them who disbelieved a painful punishment﴾, and its meaning is known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 91:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak or upon the sick﴾. The scholars differed concerning "the weak" (al-du'afa'). Some said: they are the insane (al-majanin), and weakness (al-du'f) is the deficiency of their intellects. Some said: they are the children (al-sibyan). Some said: they are the women (al-niswan). As for "the sick" (al-marda), it is well known. And His saying: ﴿nor upon those who find nothing to spend, there is no blame﴾. "Those who find nothing" are the poor (al-fuqara'), and "blame" (al-haraj) means constriction (al-diq). His saying: ﴿when they are sincere toward Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: they make their deeds sincere for Allah and for His Messenger. Sincerity of deed toward Allah is through worship, and toward the Messenger through following him. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no path against the good-doers﴾ means: there is no path (sabil) against those who do good by sincerity, and "path" here is punishment. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he recited: "And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful to the people of wrongdoing (li-ahl al-isa'a)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 92:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Nor is there blame upon those who come to you, [O Muhammad], to be provided with mounts, and you said, "I can find nothing to mount you on"﴾ mean: there is no way (against them) over the former ones nor over these. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: the verse was revealed concerning seven men, among them Abdullah ibn al-Mughaffal al-Muzani, al-Irbad ibn Sariya, and Abu (Layla) Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b. They were called the Weepers (al-Bakka'un). It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said this was said concerning Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and his companions.

There is a difference of opinion regarding His words: ﴿to be provided with mounts﴾. One of the two opinions, which is the well-known one, is that they asked for camels to ride. The second opinion is that they asked for sandals (nisal, sing. al-na'l, a sandal). This is the view of al-Hasan ibn Salih.

As for His words: ﴿"I can find nothing to mount you on." They turned away, while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief that they could not find what to spend﴾, its meaning is clear. In some reports, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "One of you will not cease to be riding as long as he is wearing sandals."

Then He said: ﴿The blame is only upon those who ask your permission while they are wealthy. They are content to be with the ones who stay behind.﴾ Al-khawalif (those who stay behind): women and children. It is said: khalif and khawalif, just as it is said: faris and fawaris, and halik and hawalik. ﴿Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.﴾ The meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 94:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿They will make excuses to you when you return to them.﴾ It is related that the hypocrites who stayed behind were some eighty-odd men. When the Messenger of Allah returned from the expedition of Tabuk, they came making excuses, so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse concerning them: ﴿Say: "Do not make excuses; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news."﴾ That is, concerning what has passed. ﴿And Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger.﴾ That is, concerning what is to come. ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾

Then He said concerning them: ﴿They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, that you may leave them alone.﴾ *Al-inqilab* (returning) is going back to the place from which they went out. ﴿So leave them alone; indeed they are filth.﴾ *Al-rijs* (filth) is stench and dirt. ﴿Their refuge is Hell, as recompense for what they used to earn.﴾

If it is said: how does He say in the verse ﴿They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, that you may leave them alone﴾ when the believers are the ones turning toward them, so that He says ﴿that you may leave them alone﴾?

The answer to this: al-Azhari mentioned in his book *al-Taqrib* the meaning of the verse: "They will swear to you by Allah for your turning away from them, so that you will turn toward them; so leave them alone."

Then He said: ﴿They will swear to you that you may be pleased with them.﴾ Al-Ridā (contentment, pleasure) is the opposite of al-Karāha (dislike). ﴿But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiant people.﴾

In the account (al-Qiṣṣa): "Abū Khaythama, a man from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, had remained behind. He had two wives. He went to them, and each of them had prepared food for him, cooled water, and spread out a mat for him in the shade. He looked at that and said: 'The Messenger of Allah is in the heat and the dust, and Abū Khaythama is in the shade! This is not fair.' Then he mounted his she-camel and set out following the Messenger of Allah. He caught up with the Prophet while he had halted at Tabūk. The people said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a rider is approaching.' The Messenger of Allah said: 'Be Abū Khaythama.' The people said: 'It is Abū Khaythama.'"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 97:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿The Bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy, and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has sent down﴾. The meaning of ajdar (more fitting, more likely) is: more inclined, and more apt that they not know the limits of what Allah has sent down ﴿to His Messenger﴾, and this is due to their remoteness from hearing the Qur'an and from knowing the sunan (the prophetic traditions and practices).

In some reports it is said: "The people of disbelief (kufur) are the people of the graves." And in the reports from the Successors (tabi'un) on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i: a Bedouin sat beside Zayd ibn Suhan, whose left hand had been struck off on the day of Nahawand in the battle against the Persians (ajam). He began to speak with him and mention knowledge to him. The Bedouin said to him: "Your knowledge comforts me, but your hand makes me uneasy." Zayd said to him: "What about my hand makes you uneasy, when it is only the left?" The Bedouin said: "I do not know whether the left is cut off or the right." Zayd ibn Suhan said: "Allah the Exalted has spoken truly: ﴿The Bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy﴾."

Zayd ibn Suhan is among the great Successors, and he is the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned concerning him that his hand would precede him into Paradise. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 98:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among the Bedouins is one who takes what he spends as a penalty﴾. Al-maghram (penalty, a loss): the undertaking of what is not obligatory. The poet said:

(So your possessions are plundered by enemies, as if you see the abandonment of Layla as a penalty, and you are its debtor.)

His saying: ﴿And awaits for you the turns of fortune﴾. That is: he waits for misfortunes to befall you. Al-dawa'ir (turns of fortune) is the plural of al-da'ira (the circle), and al-da'ira is the transfer of what is loved to what is disliked. It was also said: al-dawa'ir are the vicissitudes of time.

Then He said: ﴿Upon them is the circle of evil﴾. It was also recited as "da'iratu al-su'" (dā'iratu l-sū'). Its meaning: the great calamity is that which will overtake them. And His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 99:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾, its meaning is known. ﴿And take what they spend as means of nearness (qurubat) to Allah and invocations (salawat) of the Messenger﴾. Qurubat is the plural of qurbah (nearness), and salawat is the plural of salah (prayer/invocation). The meaning of qurubat is that he seeks nearness to Allah, may He be exalted, and the meaning of salawat is that he seeks the supplication of the Messenger of Allah.

Know that salah from Allah is mercy (rahmah), from the believers it is supplication (du'a'), and from the angels it is seeking forgiveness (istighfar). Al-A'sha said:

(She says, "My daughter, when he had drawn near to departing, ... O Lord, keep away from my father weariness and pain,")

("Upon you is like what he prayed, so close your eyes, ... for indeed the side of a man will have a resting place.")

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them into His mercy﴾, that is, into His Paradise, ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, its meaning is known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 100:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers)﴾. This verse concerns the foremost early ones (al-sabiqun al-awwalun), and regarding them there are several opinions:

One of them: the statement of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Ibn Sirin and a group, that they said: they are those who prayed towards both qiblas.

﴿The Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who followed them in excellence—Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them﴾

Ata' said: they are the people of Badr.

Al-Sha'bi said: they are the people of the Pledge of Ridwan, and the Pledge of Ridwan took place at al-Hudaybiyyah.

The fourth opinion: the foremost early ones among the Muhajirun are those who embraced Islam before the Hijrah, and the foremost early ones among the Ansar are those who pledged allegiance with the Messenger of Allah on the night of al-'Aqabah.

It is narrated from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read "wal-Ansari" in the nominative (wa-al-Ansaru) . In this reading, the foremost early ones are restricted to the Muhajirun only. The well-known reading is "wal-Ansar" (in the genitive), and its meaning is: "and of the Ansar." The Muhajirun are those who emigrated from their homelands and came to Madinah with the Messenger of Allah, and the Ansar are the people of Madinah who gave shelter to the Messenger of Allah and the Muhajirun in their homes.

As for His saying: ﴿and those who followed them in excellence﴾, there are two opinions regarding it: the first is that they are the remaining Muhajirun and Ansar other than the foremost early ones among them.

The second opinion: they are the believers until the Hour is established.

It is narrated from Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad who said: I came to Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and said to him: What is your view concerning the Companions of the Messenger of Allah? He said: All the Companions of the Messenger of Allah are in Paradise, their wrongdoers and their righteous alike. I said to him: From where do you say this? He said: Recite His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun and the Ansar﴾ up to his saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens﴾. Then he said: He made a condition for the followers, which is His saying: ﴿who followed them in excellence﴾, meaning that they followed them in their good deeds and not their bad deeds. Abu Sakhr said: It is as if I had never recited this verse at all.

In the well-known report transmitted by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not revile my Companions; by Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend gold equal to the mountain of Uhud, he would not reach the mudd of one of them, nor even half of it."

His saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾ means: Allah is pleased with them for their obedience, ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾ for His reward. The rest of the verse is known: ﴿And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 101:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have persisted in hypocrisy﴾. The people of tafsir said: They are Muzayna, Juhayna, Ashja', Ghifar and Aslam. ﴿And among the people of Madinah﴾: a people from the Aws and the Khazraj. ﴿They have persisted in hypocrisy﴾. Al-Farra' said: they have become accustomed to hypocrisy (marranu). Tha'lab said: they have become persistent in hypocrisy (istanmaru). In the verse there is inversion and rearrangement, as if He had said: "And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, who have persisted in hypocrisy, and among the people of Madinah," thus said the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani). ﴿You do not know them; We know them﴾. This is evidence that the Messenger did not know all the hypocrites.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾. Concerning this there are several opinions:

The first: it is disgrace in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.

And in a report: "The Prophet (ﷺ) stood up delivering a sermon from the pulpit and said: 'Get out, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite. Get out, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite,' and so on, until he had expelled them all from the mosque."

﴿They have mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil; perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

The second opinion: it is the view of Mujahid, that it is fear in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.

The third opinion: the first punishment is killing and the second punishment is the punishment of the grave.

The fourth: Ibn Qutaybah said: the first punishment is captivity (sabi) and the second punishment is killing.

﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾, meaning: to Hell.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 102:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, the verse. It was revealed concerning a group of the believers who stayed behind from the Messenger of God without any excuse. Among them was Abu Lubaba ibn Abd al-Mundhir and others. When the Messenger of God returned from the campaign and drew near Medina, they came and tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque, saying: "We will not release ourselves until God relents toward us." The Messenger of God entered the mosque, and it was his custom that when he went out on a journey he would pray two rak'ahs in the mosque before departing, and when he returned he would begin with the mosque and pray two rak'ahs there, and then enter his house. When he entered the mosque and saw these men tied to the pillars, he asked: "What is their situation?" It was said to him: "They have sworn that they will not release themselves until God relents toward them." The Messenger of God said: "And I swear that I will not release them until God decides concerning them by His command." So God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾. The evil deed is clearly their staying behind from the campaign. As for the righteous deed, it has two meanings:

The first: their remorse and their tying themselves to the pillars.

The second: the righteous deed is their earlier campaigns with the Messenger of God.

In the reports, on the authority of Samura ibn Jundub, the Prophet said: "Two visitors came to me during the night and set off with me to a city built of bricks of gold and bricks of silver. Men met me, half of whose creation was as beautiful as the most beautiful thing you have seen, and half of whose creation was as ugly as the ugliest thing you have seen. It was said to them: 'Go and plunge into that river,' so they plunged into the river and came out with the evil gone from them. I asked about those people, and it was said to me: 'As for the city, it is Paradise, and that is your abode. These people mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil, so God pardoned them.'"

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Perhaps God will relent toward them﴾, al-Hasan al-Basri and others said: "'Perhaps' from God is binding." So when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God ordered that those people be released from the pillars.

It is also narrated from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi that he said: "The verse I hope for most in the Qur'an is this verse."

﴿Indeed, God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 103:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow,﴾ The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: When Allah accepted the repentance of those people, they came to the Prophet with their wealth and said: "Take it as a charity for Allah." He refused to take it, so Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse: ﴿Take from their wealth.﴾ His saying ﴿purify them﴾ means: from sins. His saying ﴿and cause them to grow by it﴾ means: and elevate them by it from the ranks of the hypocrites to the ranks of the sincere. ﴿And invoke blessings upon them﴾ means: and supplicate for them. ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾ means: your supplication is a comfort for them, that is, a tranquility for them, that is, your supplication is a comfort for them, reassurance and steadfastness.

Some scholars have said: it is obligatory upon the imam to supplicate for the one who brought the charity. Others said: it is recommended, not obligatory. Others said: it is obligatory for the obligatory (zakat) and recommended for the voluntary (nafl). Others said: it is obligatory upon the imam to supplicate for the giver, and it is recommended for the poor person to supplicate. Among them is one who said: if the giver asks him to supplicate for him, it becomes obligatory; otherwise it is not obligatory.

The report has been established through the narration of Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: "When a man came to the Prophet with his charity, he would supplicate for him. My father came with his charity, and the Prophet said: 'O Allah, bless the family of Abi Awfa.'"

﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ its meaning: Ever-Knowing (ma'lum).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 104:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ — this is apparent. And His saying: ﴿and takes the charities﴾ means: He accepts the charities. Some of the scholars of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: His saying ﴿Do they not know﴾ is in the sense of a command, as if He said: "Know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants."

In the well-known and established report from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no servant gives a charity from lawful earnings — and Allah accepts only what is good — except that Allah takes it with His right hand and nurtures it, just as one of you nurtures his foal, until a morsel comes on the Day of Resurrection like Mount Uhud." Then he recited His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities﴾. And the report is sound.

It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Indeed, the charity falls into the hand of Allah before it falls into the hand of the poor person." And it is narrated in some transmissions as a marfu' report traced back to the Prophet.

His saying: ﴿And that Allah is the Most Relenting, the Most Merciful﴾ — its meaning is known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 105:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And say, "Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger and the believers."﴾ In the verse there is the meaning of warning (tahdid). If someone asks: what is the meaning of the seeing of the Messenger and the believers?

We say: The seeing of the Messenger is by Allah informing him of their deeds. The seeing of the believers is by Allah placing love in their hearts for the people of righteousness, and placing hatred in their hearts for the people of corruption.

And in some reports: "If a believer were to act within a rock that has no door, Allah would make it manifest when he has acted."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed...﴾ The verse; its meaning is known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 106:

Allah's statement: ﴿And others are deferred until Allah's command﴾. Al-irja' (deferment) means delay, and its meaning here is: deferred until Allah's command. Allah's command here means Allah's judgment (hukm).

The verse was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murara ibn al-Rabi'; these are the three men whose story will come after this.

As for His statement ﴿Either He will punish them or He will forgive them, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, its meaning is: known (ma'lum).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 107:

His exalted saying: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾. The verse was revealed concerning a group of hypocrites (munafiqun), among them: Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, Tha'labah ibn Hatib, (Jariyah ibn Yazid), his son Majma' ibn Jariyah, Hizam ibn Malik, Abu Habibah ibn al-Azar, 'Abbad ibn Hunayf, and a man called Yakhraj, totaling twelve men. They built this mosque with the intention that Allah mentioned in His Book, and that is His saying: ﴿for harm﴾, meaning: causing harm to the Messenger, ﴿and disbelief﴾ in Allah, ﴿and to cause division among the believers and as a station of preparation for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger﴾. Al-irsad (preparation) means: readiness. The one who warred against Allah and His Messenger here is Abu 'Amir the monk, who was among those who sought religion at the beginning, then he became a Christian and allied with the factions against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then he joined Caesar seeking his aid against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions. These people built this mosque and said: "We build this mosque so that we may be private, speak as we wish, and await the return of Abu 'Amir the monk." This mosque was built near the Mosque of Quba. His saying: ﴿from before﴾ refers back to Abu 'Amir. ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but goodness"﴾, meaning: nothing but gentleness toward the Muslims. ﴿And Allah testifies that indeed they are liars﴾, meaning: it is known.

Then He said: ﴿Never stand in it.﴾ It is narrated that they asked the Prophet to come and pray in it, so God Most High revealed this verse: ﴿Never stand in it.﴾ Its meaning: do not pray in it, ever. ﴿A mosque founded upon piety﴾: the scholars differed about which mosque this is. Ibn 'Umar, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: it is the Mosque of the Prophet in Medina. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated: "Two men disputed about the mosque founded upon piety, and they asked the Messenger of God, and he (ﷺ) said: 'It is this mosque of mine.'" Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi included it in his Jami'.

The second view: it is the Mosque of Quba'. This is the opinion of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada, and a group of the Successors (tabi'un).

The third view: it is all the mosques of Medina. The first view is the most correct.

His words ﴿founded upon piety﴾ mean: so that one may be protected from shirk in it. His words ﴿from the first day﴾ mean: from the beginning of the days of Islam. ﴿More worthy that you stand in it﴾ means: more deserving that you stand in it, i.e., that you pray in it. As for the words of the Most High ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves﴾, their meaning is well known.

It is narrated that the Prophet said to the people of Quba': "Indeed God Most High has praised you well; what do you do?" They said: "We perform wudu' from minor impurity and we perform ghusl from major impurity." He (ﷺ) said: "Is there anything besides this?" They said: "When one of us cleans himself after relieving himself, he likes to follow the trace of the cleansing with water." He (ﷺ) said: "That is it, so hold fast to it."

Then He said: ﴿Is he who founded his building upon piety from Allah and approval better, or he who founded his building upon the edge of a crumbling bank that collapsed with him into the fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ Some read it as "afaman assasa" (with a different reading of the first word).

﴿Is he who founded his building upon piety from Allah and approval better﴾: meaning, the one who seeks piety and seeks the approval of Allah is better.

﴿Or he who founded his building upon the edge of a crumbling bank﴾: al-shafa (the brink) is the edge and border. Al-jurf (the crumbling bank) is what has been undercut by a torrent, meaning what has been cut away by a flood, so that, because of its softness, no building can stand upon it.

His saying ﴿hār﴾ means hā'ir (crumbling), and hā'ir means fallen (collapsed).

﴿So it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell﴾: its meaning is known. ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾: its meaning is clear.

Know that the purpose of the verse is the illustration and comparison concerning the lack of stability and permanence and the evil of the outcome. Scholars differed regarding what was the outcome of the Mosque of Harm (Masjid al-Dirar). The majority hold that the Prophet (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum and 'Asim ibn 'Adi and ordered them to demolish that mosque and burn it, and they did so.

The other opinion is that the mosque collapsed on its own without anyone touching it. Some exegetical works mention that it was swallowed up into the earth. It is related that when it was swallowed up, smoke rose from it into the sky. And Allah knows best.

The Exalted said: ﴿Their building which they have built will not cease to be a cause of doubt in their hearts﴾. That is, a doubt and disquiet in their hearts. Al-Suddi said: "A burning (or inflammation) in their hearts." And His saying: ﴿unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾ has two interpretations:

One of them: until they die. In the irregular reading, it is recited: "until their hearts are cut to pieces" (ilā an taqaṭṭaʿa qulūbuhum).

The second view: until they repent, so that remorse in the heart is treated as the equivalent of a cutting within the heart.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾: All-Knowing of His creation, All-Wise in His governance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 111:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, [in exchange] for that they will have Paradise.﴾ The meaning of the verse: Allah, may He be exalted, commanded the Muslims to strive with their properties and their lives in the way of Allah, and He made Paradise their reward for it, so He placed this in the position of buying and selling.

His saying: ﴿They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise binding upon Him⁠—﴾ its meaning: the reward of Paradise is a true promise. Then He said: ﴿in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an.﴾ This is evidence that all the religious communities (ahl al-milal) were commanded to engage in jihad, and their reward was made Paradise. We have already explained the meaning of the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an.

And His saying: ﴿And who is truer to his covenant than Allah?﴾ its meaning is known. ﴿So rejoice in your transaction which you have conducted.⁠﴾ Its meaning: so be joyful in your transaction which you have conducted. ﴿And that is the great achievement.﴾

It is related in the reports that when this verse was revealed, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sale has profited; we will not cancel it, nor will we ask for its cancellation." And from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "Allah has made a bargain with you and made both transactions (al-safqatayn) for you." And from some of the Successors (tabi'un), he said: "He bought, and made the price high; and he sold, and made the exchange high." And from al-Hasan al-Basri, he said: "Allah, may He be exalted, has given you this world, so buy Paradise with some of it from Allah."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 112:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The repentant, the worshippers﴾ to the end of the verse. "The repentant" (al-tā'ibūn) are those who repented from shirk (associating partners with God). It is also said: they are those who repented from all acts of disobedience (ma'āṣī). "The worshippers" (al-'ābidūn) are those who worshipped God by affirming His oneness (tawhīd). It is also said: by all other acts of obedience (ṭā'āt).

As for ﴿the praisers﴾ (al-ḥāmidūn), there are two views:

One: they are those who praise God in every state, in ease and in hardship.

The second view: they are those who praise God for Islam.

As for His saying ﴿the wanderers﴾ (al-sā'iḥūn), there are several views:

(One) They are the fasting ones (al-ṣā'imūn). This is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas. In some reports, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The wandering (siyāḥa) of my community is fasting." Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: the fasting person was called a wanderer because he abandons food, drink and marriage.

The second view: the wanderers are those who strive in the way of God (al-mujāhidūn fī sabīl Allah). In some reports, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The wandering of my community is jihad."

The third view: the wanderers are the seekers of knowledge (ṭalabat al-'ilm). This is narrated from some of the Successors (tābi'ūn).

As for His saying ﴿the bowers, the prostrators﴾, it means: those who pray (al-muṣallūn). As for His saying ﴿those who enjoin what is right﴾, it means: those who enjoin faith (al-īmān). ﴿And those who forbid what is wrong﴾ means: those who forbid shirk. As for His saying ﴿and those who keep the limits of God﴾, its meaning is: those who uphold the commands of God. ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 113:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they should be relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾. They differed concerning the occasion of the revelation of this verse, in three opinions.

The first: what Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab related from his father: "When Abu Talib was at the point of death, the Prophet entered upon him, and with him were Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah. The Prophet said to him: 'O uncle, ﴿say: There is no god but Allah,' a word by which I can argue on your behalf before Allah.' Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn [Abi] Umayyah said to him: 'Will you turn away from the religion of Abd al-Muttalib?' They kept speaking to him until the last word he said was: 'On the religion of Abd al-Muttalib.' The Prophet said: 'I will surely ask forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from it.' So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse: ﴿It is not for the Prophet...﴾ to the end of the verse."

The second: Masruq related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "The Prophet went out to the graveyard and we followed him. He came to a grave and sat beside it, and he conversed privately for a long time. Then he wept, and we wept at his weeping. We said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, who is the owner of this grave?' He said: 'This is my mother, Aminah bint Wahb. I asked my Lord for permission to visit her, and He permitted me. Then I asked Him for permission to ask forgiveness for her, and He did not permit me.' He said: 'Compassion for her overtook me, such as a child feels for his mother, so I wept.' And Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse: ﴿It is not for the Prophet﴾ to the end of the verse."

The third opinion: it is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "He heard a man asking forgiveness for his two parents while they were polytheists. Ali said to him: 'Do you ask forgiveness for the polytheists?' That man said: 'Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father, and he was a polytheist.' So he came to the Prophet and informed him of that, and Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse in its entirety."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 114:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And the prayer-for-forgiveness of Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾. Regarding this verse there are two opinions.

The first: Abraham, peace be upon him, said to his father: "I will surely ask forgiveness for you." He said this out of hope that God Most High would bring him from disbelief to Islam, through the blessing of his supplication and his seeking forgiveness.

The second opinion: Abraham's father promised Abraham and said: "Surely I will embrace Islam, so ask forgiveness for me," and Abraham asked forgiveness for him for this reason.

﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God﴾ by his dying in disbelief, ﴿he disassociated himself from him﴾. If someone says: how is it permissible for Abraham to seek forgiveness for a polytheist? The answer: some scholars of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: it is possible that Abraham's father had outwardly displayed Islam while inwardly concealing disbelief, so Abraham asked forgiveness for him because of his outward display of Islam. ﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God﴾, persisting in disbelief inwardly, ﴿he disassociated himself from him﴾. This is what some scholars of the meanings said.

What the majority of the exegetes hold is what we have explained earlier.

Al-Hasan al-Basri recited: "إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه" (except from a promise he had made to him), and this is explicit that the promise came from Abraham. The evidence that Abraham asked forgiveness for him while he was a polytheist is that God Most High said in Surah al-Mumtahanah: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him... ﴾ up to His saying: ﴿except for the statement of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you"﴾. So He declared explicitly that Abraham is not an example in this seeking of forgiveness; rather, he sought forgiveness for him while he was a polytheist because of the promise, in hope that he would become a Muslim.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was ʾawwah, forbearing﴾, the exegetes differed concerning "ʾawwah" in several sayings.

It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Abdullah ibn Abbas that the ʾawwah is the one who supplicates much (al-du'a'). And from Ibn Mas'ud in another narration: that it is the merciful (al-rahim). And from Ibn Abbas in another narration: that it is the believing, repentant one (al-mu'min al-tawwab). And from Mujahid: that it is the jurist (al-faqih). And from Ka'b al-Ahbar: that it is the one who groans over sins, saying: "Awwah, awwah." Abu Dharr narrated that "a man used to circumambulate the Ka'bah saying: 'Awwah, awwah.' I said to the Prophet: 'This man is harming us,' and he said: 'Do not say that, for he is an awwah.'" The poet said:

(When I rise to saddle her at night... she groans the groan of a sorrowful man)

And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: the ʾawwah is the one who glorifies God (al-musabbih). It was also said: it is the one who stands in station (al-mawqif). It was also said: it is the one who is certain (al-muqin).

As for al-Halim: it is the one who pardons sins (al-safuh 'an al-dhunub).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verses 115–116:

God's words: ﴿And it is not for God to lead a people astray after He has guided them﴾. Its meaning: God would not decree misguidance by their abandoning the commands, ﴿until He makes clear to them what they should be wary of﴾, so that they would abandon [those commands].

And it is related from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' (a Basran grammarian and reader of the Qur'an) that he said: its meaning is: until He establishes proof against them through the command.

The occasion of revelation of the verse: a people had come to the Prophet and embraced Islam, and wine had not yet been prohibited nor the qibla changed. They returned to their people while still upon that state. Then wine was prohibited and the qibla was changed, and they had no knowledge of this. When they later came to Madina, they found that wine had been prohibited and the qibla changed, so they said to the Prophet: "You were upon a religion and we were upon other than it, so are we astray?" Then God revealed: ﴿And it is not for God to lead a people astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should be wary of﴾.

There is another view regarding the verse: that it concerns seeking forgiveness for the polytheists. For a group of the Companions had asked forgiveness for their fathers and did not know that this was not permissible. When the prohibition concerning it was revealed, they feared greatly for themselves; so God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

God's words: ﴿Indeed, God is All-Knowing of everything﴾. Likewise, the verse that follows it is clear in its meaning up to its end.
