Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 117:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Muhajirun and the Ansar﴾. The meaning of His words ﴿Indeed Allah has turned﴾ is: indeed Allah has overlooked [their fault]. It has also been said: indeed Allah has pardoned [them].

His words ﴿who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾ mean: at the time of hardship. The Battle of Tabuk was called the Battle of Hardship (ghazwat al-'usrah), and likewise that army was called the Army of Hardship (jaysh al-'usrah). Al-'usrah (hardship) means severe difficulty. They faced hardship in mounts, provisions and water. It is related that two or three persons, or more, would take turns riding a single camel. It is also related that their provisions ran out, so that two men would share a single date between them. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas. It is also related that they suffered such severe thirst that they slaughtered the camels, squeezed their stomachs and drank what was in them. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) asked Allah for water, and they were given drink. This is how 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) related it. This is the meaning of hardship.

His words ﴿after the hearts of a group of them had nearly swerved﴾. It is read as "tazigh" and "yazigh". Whoever reads "tazigh" refers it to the hearts (qulub), and whoever reads "yazigh" refers it to the verb (al-fi'l), as if he said: the act swerves, [namely] the hearts of a group of them.

As for zaygh (swerving) in the language, it is inclination (al-mayl). The inclination intended here is not inclination away from the religion; rather, the intended inclination is inclination away from following the Messenger of Allah and supporting him in the expedition, and choosing to stay behind because of the severity of the hardship.

﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness﴾. If someone says: what is this repetition, since He said at the beginning of the verse: ﴿Indeed Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet﴾?

The answer to this: He mentioned the turning (tawbah) at the beginning of the verse before mentioning the sin, and it was a pure favour (tafaddul) from Allah. When He mentioned the sin, He repeated the mention of the turning, and what is meant by it is acceptance (al-qabul).

﴿Indeed He is Kind and Merciful to them﴾. Its meaning is known.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 118:

The words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿And [He turned in forgiveness] to the three who were left behind﴾. Ikrimah ibn Ammar recited "wa-ʿalā al-thalāthati alladhīna khullifū" (وعَلى الثَّلَاثَة الَّذين خلفوا) as mukhaffaf (lightened, with the letter not doubled). In some qira'at (recitations), it is read "wa-ʿalā al-thalāthati alladhīna khālafū" (وعَلى الثَّلَاثَة الَّذين خالفوا), with "khālafū" in place of "khullifū".

Know that these three are the ones concerning whom God, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And [there are] others deferred until God's command﴾. As for their names: Kaʿb ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murara ibn ﴿Despite its vastness, and their souls became confining for them﴾ al-Rabiʿ. They were sincere believers who stayed behind without an excuse. When the Prophet came to Madina, returning from the expedition of Tabuk, they came to him and acknowledged their sin in his presence, and that they had no excuse. So he deferred their matter, did not seek forgiveness for them, and forbade the Muslims from associating with them and speaking to them.

There is a long account of this verse in the "Sahihayn" (the two Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim). It is narrated that they remained in this state for forty nights. Then the Messenger of God ordered them to keep away from their wives until the completion of fifty nights. The companions of the Messenger of God would greet them, but they would not return the greeting. Kaʿb ibn Malik said: "I used to enter the mosque and pray, and look to see whether the Messenger of God was looking at me. Whenever I looked at him, he turned his gaze away from me." He said: "One day I broke into the orchard of Abu Qatada, who was my paternal cousin, and I greeted him, but he did not return my greeting. So I said to him: 'O cousin, do you know that I love God and His Messenger?' He remained silent. I repeated my words three times, and on the third time he said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' So I wept intensely and left." He said: "When the fiftieth night was complete, since the Messenger of God had forbidden us from speaking, I was on the roof of my house after I had prayed the dawn prayer, and I was in the state God mentioned: ﴿until, when the earth was confining for them despite its vastness﴾, that is, despite its spaciousness and breadth, ﴿and their souls were confining for them﴾, that is, because of the estrangement of the people and the harshness of the Messenger of God toward them. Then I heard a caller calling from the summit of Sal‘ — and sal‘ is a mountain — 'Good news, O Kaʿb ibn Malik!' He said: 'I fell down in prostration to God. The bearer of good news came, and I gave him my garment, and I put on two other garments. I went to the Messenger of God and sat before him, and his face was shining like the brightness of the moon. He said: "Rejoice, O Kaʿb ibn Malik, at the best day that has passed over you since you embraced Islam." I said: "O Messenger of God, is this from you or from God?" He said: "No, rather it is from God," and he recited the verse to me. I said: "O Messenger of God, part of my repentance is that I should relinquish all (of) my wealth as charity for God and His Messenger." He said: "Keep some of your wealth for yourself; it is better for you."' " The narration continues to its end.

As for the words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿and they thought there was no refuge from God except in Him﴾, its meaning is: "and they thought," that is, they were certain, "that there is no place of refuge and no escape from God except to Him."

As for the words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent﴾, meaning: that they might remain steadfast in repentance and be firm upon it, for their repentance had already been decreed. ﴿Indeed, God is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾, whose meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 119:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾ Al-Dahhak said: "With Muhammad and his companions."

It is related from some of them that he said: "With the truthful" means: with Abu Bakr and Umar. And from some of them: "With the four rightly-guided caliphs." And some of them said: The truthful here are the three who were mentioned earlier, for they were truthful with the Prophet by confessing their sin, and they did not offer false excuses like the hypocrites. It is related from Ka'b ibn Malik that he said: "Allah has not tested me with any trial greater in my view than my truthfulness to the Messenger of Allah, for part of my gratitude for it is that I never lie again, ever." It is related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Lying is not fitting in earnest or in jest," and he recited this verse. And it is said that in his recitation it was: "and be among the truthful."

"The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿It was not [proper] for the people of Madinah and those of the bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah﴾, to the end of the verse. Its meaning: it is a prohibition against staying behind.

And His words: ﴿nor to prefer themselves over his own self﴾ mean: it was not for them to choose ease and comfort and to leave the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the hardship of the journey and the toil of exertion.

Then He said: ﴿That is because they will not suffer thirst﴾. Ẓama'(thirst): thirst. ﴿nor fatigue﴾. Naṣab (fatigue): exhaustion. ﴿nor hunger﴾, which is famine, ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, that is, in jihad.

And His words: ﴿nor do they tread a path that angers the disbelievers﴾ meaning: they do not set foot anywhere that enrages the disbelievers, ﴿nor do they gain from an enemy any gain﴾ meaning: they do not inflict upon them anything, whether in person or in property, ﴿except that a righteous deed is recorded for them thereby. Indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost﴾. Its meaning is clear."

Then He said: ﴿And they spend no expenditure, small or large﴾, meaning: little or much. It was said in the exegesis: even a date. ﴿Nor do they cross a valley﴾, meaning: they do not traverse a valley, going forward or returning, ﴿except that it is recorded for them﴾, meaning: they are rewarded for that, ﴿so that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾. Its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 122:

The words of God Most High: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾ — the verse — and in it there are two opinions:

The first: "The Prophet used to send out expeditions (sariyya, small raiding parties) after the Battle of Tabuk, and the people would all go out, due to the great shame and blame they had suffered for having stayed behind. So God Most High revealed this verse." Qatadah said: This applies to the expeditions; as for when the Messenger himself goes out, they are obliged to go out with him all together.

The second opinion: The Prophet supplicated against Mudar and said: "O God, make their years like the years of Joseph." He said: So a severe drought and famine struck them, and the tribes kept coming to Medina in their entirety, saying: "We have embraced Islam." They were crowding the people of Medina in their dwellings and fouling the roads, so God Most High revealed this verse, and the Messenger of God sent them back to their tribes.

As for His words: ﴿Why should not a group from every section of them go forth﴾, its meaning is: Why did not a group from every section of them go forth? According to the first opinion, the meaning of the verse is a prohibition against leaving the Messenger of God alone. As for His words: ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, it means: that they may attend the descent of the Qur'an and the explanation of the Sunnah (sunan, prophetic practices). ﴿and warn their people when they return to them﴾ means: that the expedition, when it returns to them, may inform them of what has been revealed of the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

According to the second opinion, the meaning of the verse is: It is not for the people of the tribes to go forth all together to Medina and abandon their places; rather, let a group from every section go forth, i.e., from every tribe a group, so that they may gain understanding in the religion, warn their people, and teach their people when they return to them. ﴿So that they may beware⦆.

As for "ṭā'ifa" (group): it is a term for three or more, though the word has occurred in the Qur'an referring to one person, and we have mentioned this in His words: ﴿If We pardon one group of you﴾ earlier.

The scholars of legal theory (ahl al-uṣūl) have used this verse as evidence for the obligation of accepting the report of a single narrator (khabar al-wāḥid), and the question in the legal theory literature is a great one (kabīra).

As for "fiqh" (jurisprudence), linguistically it is an expression for understanding; in the sharia it is an expression for a specific knowledge, namely the knowledge of the rulings.

It has been established from the Prophet that he said: "Whoever God intends good for, He gives him understanding of the religion."

It is also related from the Prophet that he said: "People are mines; the best of them in the Jahiliyya are the best of them in Islam when they gain understanding." And in some reports: "The best worship is fiqh, and one learned jurist is more severe upon Satan than a thousand worshippers." And it is related from al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Seeking knowledge is better than voluntary prayer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 123:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers﴾, meaning: those who are near you. And from ʿUmar: they are the Daylam. And from others: they are the Romans. ﴿And let them find in you harshness﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: courage. And al-Hasan said: patience in war. ﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous﴾, is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 124:

The Most High said: ﴿And when a surah is sent down, among them are those who say, "Which of you has had its faith increased by this?"﴾ This refers to the hypocrites (munafiqun) who used to say this statement mockingly. Then Allah the Most High said: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice﴾, meaning they are delighted.

Then He said: ﴿As for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, that is, doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿it adds to them uncleanness upon their uncleanness, and they die while they are disbelievers﴾, that is, disbelief upon their disbelief.

If someone says: How does the revelation of the surah increase them in disbelief?

The answer: They used to disbelieve in every surah that God Most High revealed. So when they disbelieved at the revelation of a surah, their disbelief was attributed to it. This is like the Arabs saying: "Sufficient as a disease is safety (kafa bil-salama da')", because the disease occurs after a long period of safety. The poet said:

(I see my sight has troubled me after health... and it is enough of a disease for you that you be healthy and safe)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 126:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year?﴾ Its meaning: they are afflicted every year with illnesses and hardships. It was also said: [they are tested] with jihad against the enemies. ﴿Then they do not repent﴾: they do not return to Allah. ﴿Nor do they take heed﴾: nor do they admonish themselves.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 127:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when a surah is sent down, some of them look at others, [asking], "Does anyone see you?"﴾ (the verse). The hypocrites, when a surah or some part of the Qur'an was revealed, would gesture to one another, while fearing at the same time that the believers would see them. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Does anyone see you?﴾ Then He said: ﴿Then they turn away.﴾ In this there are two meanings. One: they turned away from their places. The other: they turned away from faith, meaning they did not believe and did not accept.

As for His saying: ﴿Allah has turned their hearts away﴾, Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: Allah misguided them as a recompense for their disbelief. ﴿Because they are a people who do not comprehend﴾ — its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 128:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾. It is reported as an irregular (shadhdh) reading: "min anfusikum" (with the fa' vowelled with a fatha, i.e. "min anfasikum"). It is said that this reading is the reading of Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her. Ya'qub al-Hadrami said: "I sought this letter for fifty years and did not find a single narrator for it." The meaning of this is: the most noble of you and the best of you.

The well-known reading is ﴿from among yourselves﴾. Qatadah said: its meaning is that his lineage is well known among you.

The second view: it is related from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: ﴿from among yourselves﴾ means that he was not born except from a valid marriage, back to the time of Adam.

The third view: it is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: its meaning is that there is no tribe of the Arabs except that the Prophet has been born to it.

The fourth view: the meaning of this is the meaning of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you﴾. And when the Messenger is a human being like the people, he is closer to familiarity and nearer to understanding the proof.

As for His statement: ﴿It grieves him that you suffer hardship﴾, i.e. his suffering of your hardship is difficult for him. Al-'anat (hardship) is that which is disliked and the encounter of hardship. It is as if He said: it is grievous to him what harms you and destroys you, which is the disbelief you are upon.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Ardently desirous of you﴾. Al-hirs (ardent desire) is the intensity of seeking a thing. Its meaning: ardently desirous for your faith. ﴿Toward the believers, full of kindness and mercy﴾: compassionate and gentle.

Allah, exalted is He, has given him in this verse two of His names, and this is at the peak of honour.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 9, verse 129:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, its meaning: if they turn away from faith or from you. ﴿Say: Allah is sufficient for me﴾, that is, Allah suffices me (kafi Allah, al-kafi meaning the one who suffices). ﴿There is no deity except Him. Upon Him I have relied﴾, upon Him I have depended and in Him I have trusted. ﴿And He is the Lord of the Great Throne﴾. Ibn Muhaysin recited "Rabb al-'Arsh al-'Azim" with a raised (nominative) vowel, so it refers back to Allah exalted is He, whereas the well-known reading with a kasra (genitive) refers back to the Throne (al-'Arsh). It is reported from one of the Successors (al-Tabi'un): "No one knows the extent of the Throne except Allah exalted is He." In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) it is said that he said: "The Throne is of a red ruby." It is reported from Wahb ibn Munabbih that Allah exalted is He created the Throne from His light. It is reported from Ka'b al-Ahbar that the heavens within the Throne are like a lamp suspended from the sky. It is reported from Mujahid that the heavens within the Throne are like a ring. It is related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he said concerning these two verses: they are the most recent verses revealed concerning Allah in terms of their final revelation. Accordingly, on his view, these two verses are the last of what was revealed of the Qur'an. This is also a report from Ibn 'Abbas. We have mentioned other than this through the narration of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib. And Allah knows best what is correct.
